broad-ecosystem-inventory-wildlife-habit.d:
The Broad Ecosystem Inventory (BEI) Classification provides broad regional information about the distribution of ecosystems throughout the province and the value of these ecosystems to wildlife. This work is done in order to facilitate the use of wildlife information in broad provincial and regional land and resource planning initiatives. Broad Ecosystem Units are mapped based on imagery of the provincial land base generally captured at a scale of 1:250,000. BEI mapping represents forest conditions from approximately 1995 to 2000.

The BEI Classification was used to produce wildlife habitat capability and suitability mapping following Provincial Wildlife Habitat Ratings (WHR) Standards (Resource Inventory Committee 1999). Habitat classifications were based on BEI units. BEI units were evaluated and rated to determine the habitat potential (capability) and current habitat conditions (suitability) for selected wild ungulates and furbearers within each seral stage within each Broad Ecosystem Unit (and related site modifier variation) within the framework of Ecosections and Biogeoclimatic Sub-zone/Variants for their ability to supply the species’ necessary life requisites. Regional Wildlife and Habitat biologists, technicians, Forest Ecosystem Specialists, and consulting species experts provided species habitat ratings for each region of the province.

broad-ecosystem-inventory-wildlife-habit.m: BEI originated in 1985 as Preliminary Biophysical Mapping produced to meet strategic level planning and wildlife conservation needs. In the early 1990’s this mapping was renamed Broad Ecosystem Inventory. During the 1990s BEI was mapped a number of times due to improved imagery, changes in ecological classifications, and faulty data produced by various mapping contractors. BEI reflects forest seral stages as was present from 1995 to 2000. BEI incorporated versions of two other provincial ecosystem classifications – Ecoregion Classification and Biogeoclimatic Ecosystem Classification - that were current during the 1995-2000 period. BEI also used Ministry of Forest’s MapGen Forest Cover (generalised forest cover) product to inform BEI mapping. building-permits-bper-.d:
Building permit data and highlights report for Canada and British Columbia, including permit values and number of residential units created. British Columbia data is available at the census division and census subdivision levels. Annual data for British Columbia is available at the economic region level. The monthly dataset covers the period from January 2003 to July 2026, and the highlights report covers data from January 2025 to July 2026. Annual data is available for 2003 to 2025.

Note: Due to changes in methodology, there is a data break between 2003–2017 and January 2018 onward. Therefore, these data are not directly comparable. Additionally, for 2003 to 2017, monthly data by residential unit type at the CD and CSD levels are not available and therefore only total residential units are included in this file.

The Building Permits (BPER) survey is a key indicator of building activity; however, some data, particularly at more granular geographic levels, may be of lower quality. Users are advised to exercise caution when interpreting this data. For the most accurate and specific building permit information, please refer directly to the relevant municipality. Although widely used as a leading indicator, BPER data does not capture all construction activity in the province, as not all areas report and some large projects do not require a permit. In some cases, the value of permits and units shown in this data is less than actual due to incomplete reporting by …

The Canadian National Wetland Inventory (CNWI) is an initiative to compile, process, and publish the best available wetland mapping, field validation data, and metadata, into comprehensive publicly available geodatabases. It also aims to acquire additional wetland data to fill high priority gaps in coverage, with an emphasis on peatlands and coastal wetlands. The CNWI polygonal geodatabase, user manual and metadata are available for download on the Government of Canada’s Open Data Portal for use in geographic information system (GIS) software programs, https://open.canada.ca/en/open-data.

The CNWI British Columbia (CNWI-BC) version of the CNWI geodatabase includes all the BC-based wetland data found in the national CNWI geodatabase as well as additional detail on various wetland properties as described in various BC classification systems including: Biogeoclimatic Ecosystem Classification (BEC) and Terrestrial Ecosystems Information (TEI). The CNWI-BC geodatabase also includes additional project identifier fields to ensure seamless integration with provincial database standards (RISC 2023). All CNWI wetland inventory projects in BC should be completed to CNWI-BC standard. CWS Pacific will integrate new CNWI-BC data to the CNWI (national) schema periodically.

Current version: v14 (2026-07-20)

canadian-rental-housing-index.d:
The Canadian Rental Housing Index (http://rentalhousingindex.ca/) is a comprehensive database of rental housing statistics, providing information for renter households in over 800 municipalities and regional districts across B.C. and the rest of Canada. All of the information contained in the Index is derived from a Statistics Canada custom tabulation based on the 2016 and 2021 long-form census.

The Index includes various data for renter households, such as:

* Average and median incomes
* Average rents
* Renter households spending 30% and 50% or more of their income on shelter
* Income quartiles
* Bedroom sizes
* Suitability (overcrowding)
* Demographic information for Indigenous renters, families, seniors and youth, and immigrants

cariboo-consolidated-roads.d:
This dataset contains roads in the Cariboo Natural Resource Region that have undergone an ortho-verification process. This process entailed a manual review of every road segment against high resolution satellite imagery to determine a) if the road exists or not and b) if the road linework is in the correct location. Road locations were corrected as required. Roads that were visible on the satellite imagery but missing from the road dataset were digitized (added in) and roads that were not visible on the satellite imagery were flagged as not existing and removed from this published dataset. Additionally, if an assessor was unable to determine whether a road existed or not based on the satellite imagery the road was flagged for a future field-based assessment. As of April 2025 this field-based assessment is not complete.

A field called [ROAD_TENURE_TYPE] identifies the administrative responsibility for each road, and was filled out based on several publicly available road datasets. Where there is a discrepancy between the information in this dataset and the source dataset(s), the source dataset(s) should be considered the authoritative source.

Source datasets include:

Forest Tenure Road Section Lines: https://catalogue.data.gov.bc.ca/dataset/243c94a1-f275-41dc-bc37-91d8a2b26e10

Ministry of Transportation (MOT) Road Features Inventory (RFI): https://catalogue.data.gov.bc.ca/dataset/e37cc64b-41a6-491f-be3b-9983bd5948f7

caribou-herd-locations-for-bc.d:
This data contains the current caribou subpopulation (herd) boundaries. Herd boundaries are derived from the best available science and expert knowledge. A caribou subpopulation (herd) boundary is the area required to be managed to achieve a self-sustaining population. Subpopulation boundaries do not overlap even though some caribou subpopulations share portions of their annual range.

*This dataset is the focal point of the Caribou in British Columbia - Web Application .

c: A system generated idenfitier to insure row uniqueness.
The Caribou Herd Tag is a business identifier for the Caribou population unit. It consists of a region or a place name in close proximity to the herd.
The herd number is a short alphnumeric value assigned to each herd.
HERD STATUS field is for indicating whether the polygon defines a caribou herd, trace occurrence, or extirpated area.
The herd name is a user identifier for the herd name. It consists primarily of placenames but can also include the names of individuals.
The ecology type (ECOTYPE) is a classification of the ecology of the regions where the herd exists

The risk status is the level of risk that the caribou herd is experiencing at present. It consists of a two character code that is drawn from the RISK STATUS domain. The RISK STATUS domain contains the following codes and descriptions:EN: EndangeredNAR:Not at riskTR: TracesNU: Not Used
ESTIMATED CARIBOU POPULATION contains the estimated Caribou population in a particular herd.
YEAR OF LAST SURVEY: contains the year that Caribou population was surveyed.

A feature code is most importantly a means of linking a feature to its name and definition. For example, the code GB15300120 on a digital geographic feature links it to the name "Lake - Dry" with the definition "A lake bed from which all water has drained or evaporated."
GEOMETRY is the column used to reference the spatial coordinates defining the feature.
OBJECTID is a required attribute of feature classes and object classes in a geodatabase.

cciss-environmental-suitability-ratings-.d:
This dataset contains the environmental suitability ratings of tree species for British Columbia and adjacent jurisdictions (Northwestern United States and Alberta) at a site series level. These ordinal ratings (E1-5) reflect the probability for successful establishment and growth of a species across the entire environmental space of a site series in the baseline (pre-climate change) climate normal period of 1961-90. The environmental suitability ratings focus on how well the species is suited to the climatic and site (i.e. edaphic) conditions of a site series regardless of management objective.

Tree species environmental suitability ratings refer to the degree to which a tree species can be successfully established and maintained to maturity under specific climatic & edaphic conditions in the absence of independent limiting factors such as biotic (e.g. forest health) or abiotic (e.g. fire) disturbances. The baseline environmental suitability does not include regions where a species is absent in natural stands due to non-climatic or site level factors such as unfavourable disturbance regimes or migration lags.

Please see Data Dictionary for important information on data use.

cciss-western-north-america-bec-tables.d:
These data tables describe biogeoclimatic units for Western North America. These data were assembled as inputs to the Climate Change Informed Species Selection (CCISS) framework.

The CCISS framework is built on Biogeoclimatic Ecosystem Classification (BEC). CCISS uses spatial climatic analogs (BEC subzone/variants) to make inferences about future tree species suitability, known as biogeoclimatic projections. Creating species suitability projections for the future climates of British Columbia requires finding climate analogs in Alberta and the Western US. For Alberta, we adapted the Ecological Classification of Alberta (e.g., Archibald et al. 1996), with 21 natural subregions (Natural Regions Committee 2006) as the biogeoclimatic map units and 167 ecological sites as the site series units. For Washington, Idaho, Montana, Oregon, northern California, and northwestern Wyoming, we use a draft biogeoclimatic ecosystem classification for the Western US developed by Del Meidinger and Will MacKenzie. Biogeoclimatic units are detailed in the: Western North America Biogeoclimatic Units Attribute Table.

The CCISS tool predicts climate change implications to tree species environmental suitability at a site series level. We have compiled sites series information for Western North America biogeoclimatic units, detailed in; Site Series Information Table and Edatopic Space Table.

census-agricultural-regions-all-years-.d:
Census agricultural regions (CARs) are composed of groups of adjacent census divisions and are used by the Census of Agriculture to disseminate agricultural statistics.

This dataset contains the CAR boundaries for all censuses, from the 2021 Canada census onwards.

Source: Dictionary, Census of Population, 2021 (https://www12.statcan.gc.ca/census-recensement/2021/ref/dict/az/Definition-eng.cfm?ID=geo006)

These data for statistical areas are updated using the results of the previous census, as well as input from users.

census-consolidated-subdivisions-all-yea.d: A census consolidated subdivision (CCS) is a statistical area of aggregated census subdivisions used by the Census of Agriculture. A census consolidated subdivision is a grouping of adjacent census subdivisions. Generally, the smaller more urban census subdivisions (towns, villages, etc.) are combined with the surrounding, larger, more rural census subdivision, in order to create a geographic level between the census subdivision and the census division. The dataset contains all census years from 2006 to 2016.
census-consolidated-subdivisions-all-yea.m: The geographic area boundaries, names, codes, and the relationships among the various geographic levels are found on Statistics Canada?s Spatial Data Infrastructure (SDI). These data for administrative areas are updated using information from provincial and territorial sources. These data for statistical areas are updated using the results of the previous census, as well as input from users.

c: CENSUS YEAR is the year the national census in Canada was conducted, e.g., 2006, 2011. This is done every five years by Statistics Canada.

CENSUS CONSOLIDATED ID - Uniquely identifies an census consolidated subdivision (composed of the 2-digit province/territory code and the 2-digit census division code and the 3 digit census consolidated subdivision code)
CENSUS CONSOLIDATED NAME - The name of the census consolidated subdivision
GEOMETRY is the column used to reference the spatial coordinates defining the feature.

census-dissemination-areas-all-years-.d: Please note this data is only licensed for use by specific government agencies. The Dissemination Area Boundary Files portray the dissemination area boundaries all census years from 2006 to 2016. A dissemination area is a small area composed of one or more neighbouring blocks and is the smallest standard geographic area for which all census data are disseminated. The digital boundary file contains the boundaries of the over 54 thousand dissemination areas which combined cover all of Canada. The cartographic boundary file contains the boundaries of over 54 thousand dissemination areas. Dissemination areas 59290104 and 59290108 are not included within the cartographic boundary file because they are located entirely within coastal waters, they are therefore automatically removed during the production of the cartographic boundary file.

These data for statistical areas are updated using the results of the previous census, as well as input from users.

CENSUS SUBDIVISION ID - Uniquely identifies a census subdivision (composed of the 2-digit province/territory code, the 2-digit census division code, and the 3-digit census subdivision code)

CENSUS CONSOLIDATED ID - Uniquely identifies a census consolidated subdivision (composed of the 2-digit province/territory code, the 2-digit census division code and the 3-digit census consolidated subdivision code)
CENSUS DIVISION ID - Uniquely identifies a census division (composed of the 2-digit province/territory code and the 2-digit census division code)
ECONOMIC REGION ID - Uniquely identifies an economic region (composed of the 2-digit province/territory code and the 2-digit economic region code)
CENSUS TRACT ID - Uniquely identifies a census tract (composed of the 3-digit census metroppolitan area/census agglomeration code followed by the 7-character CTNAME)
CENSUS METRO AREA ID - Uniquely identifies a census metropolitan area or census agglomeration.
GEOMETRY is the column used to reference the spatial coordinates defining the feature.

census-division-boundaries-all-years-.d: A census division is an administrative area, which is a component of the Standard Geographical Classification and comprised of census subdivisions. Census division is the general term for provincially legislated areas (such as regional municipality and regional district) or their equivalents. Census divisions are intermediate geographic areas between the province or territorial level and the municipality (census subdivision). The dataset contains all census years from 2006 to 2016.

census-metropolitan-areas-all-years-.d: A census metropolitan area (CMA) or a census agglomeration (CA) is formed by one or more adjacent municipalities centred on a large urban area (known as the urban core). The census population count of the urban core is at least 10,000 to form a census agglomeration and at least 50,000 to form a census metropolitan area. The dataset contains all census years from 2006 to 2016.
census-metropolitan-areas-all-years-.m: The geographic area boundaries, names, codes, and the relationships among the various geographic levels are found on Statistics Canada?s Spatial Data Infrastructure (SDI). These data for administrative areas are updated using information from provincial and territorial sources. These data for statistical areas are updated using the results of the previous census, as well as input from users.

Comprehensive set of census profile attributes for census divisions, including attributes describing population age, housing and shelter, spoken languages, occupations and labour, industry, commuting, education, and industry.

c: CEN_CPCCS_SYSID is a system generated unique identification number.
CENSUS_YEAR is the year in which the census was conducted. In Canada, censuses are conducted every 5 years.
CENSUS_SUBDIVISION_ID is a unique numerical identifier assigned to a census subdivision, e.g., 5901023.
CENSUS_SUBDIVISION_NAME is the name of the census subdivision to which these dimension values pertain.
CENSUS SUBDIVISION TYPE - Census subdivisions (CSDs) are classified into 55 types according to official designations adopted by provincial/territorial or federal authorities.
CENSUS SUBDIVISION TYPE DESC contains the full description of the census subdivision type for the record.

GLOBAL_NONRESP_LF_PCT is the Global non-response rate for the long form census, described in the document http://www12.statcan.gc.ca/census-recensement/2016/ref/98-304/chap11-eng.cfm.

census-profiles-for-bc-census-subdivisio.d:
Comprehensive set of census profile attributes for census subdivisions, including attributes describing population age, housing and shelter, spoken languages, occupations and labour, industry, commuting, education, and industry.

Data elements in this view will be populated as data becomes available from Stats Canada (see Release Schedule - 2021 Census dissemination planning (https://www12.statcan.gc.ca/census-recensement/2021/ref/prodserv/release-diffusion-eng.cfm)

files.n: Characteristic values for Canada Census 2021 of Population - Census Subdivisions

c: CEN_CPCCS_SYSID is a system generated unique identification number.
CENSUS_YEAR is the year in which the census was conducted. In Canada, censuses are conducted every 5 years.
CENSUS_SUBDIVISION_ID is a unique numerical identifier assigned to a census subdivision, e.g., 5901023.
CENSUS_SUBDIVISION_NAME is the name of the census subdivision to which these dimension values pertain.
CENSUS SUBDIVISION TYPE - Census subdivisions (CSDs) are classified into 55 types according to official designations adopted by provincial/territorial or federal authorities.
CENSUS SUBDIVISION TYPE DESC contains the full description of the census subdivision type for the record.
GLOBAL_NONRESP_SF_PCT is the Global non-response rate for the short form census, described in the document http://www12.statcan.gc.ca/census-recensement/2021/ref/98-304/chap11-eng.cfm.
GLOBAL_NONRESP_LF_PCT is the Global non-response rate for the long form census, described in the document http://www12.statcan.gc.ca/census-recensement/2021/ref/98-304/chap11-eng.cfm.

census-profiles-for-bc-provincial-electo.d:
Compilations of descriptive statistics from the Census of Population specific to British Columbia and each of its provincial electoral districts. These semi-custom Census Profiles include statistics describing age and gender, families and household types, housing, labour and income, immigration and citizenship, mobility and migration, commuting and place of work, education, ethnocultural and religious diversity, and languages (see Related Links for more information).

All statistics are based on Census data tabulations produced by Statistics Canada. Census Profiles are specific to a Census release year and electoral district boundary set; by law, provincial electoral districts are subject to boundary changes after every second provincial general election. The combinations of Census year and electoral boundaries redistribution covered by this dataset include:

- 2016 Census, 2015 Electoral Boundaries Redistribution (87 districts)

- 2021 Census, 2023 Electoral Boundaries Redistribution (93 districts)

As an alternative to the CSV data files, 2021 Census Profile summary reports by individual electoral district in PDF format can be accessed from the Legislative Library of British Columbia website (see Related Links).

If you need help with this dataset, you can reach BC Stats at the email below; however, submitting a support request is recommended.

census-subdivision-boundaries-all-years-.d: A census subdivision is an administrative area, which is a component of the Standard Geographical Classification. Census subdivision is the general term for municipalities, as determined by provincial legislation, or areas treated as municipal equivalents for statistical purposes, for example, Indian reserves, Indian settlements and unorganized territories. The dataset contains all census years from 2006 to 2016.
census-subdivision-boundaries-all-years-.m: The geographic area boundaries, names, codes, and the relationships among the various geographic levels are found on Statistics Canada?s Spatial Data Infrastructure (SDI). These data for administrative areas are updated using information from provincial and territorial sources. These data for statistical areas are updated using the results of the previous census, as well as input from users.

c: CENSUS YEAR is the year the national census in Canada was conducted, e.g., 2006, 2011. This is done every five years by Statistics Canada.
CENSUS SUBDIVISION ID uniquely identifiers a census subdivision (composed of 2-digit province code, 2-digit census division and 3-digit census subdivision codes)
CENSUS SUBDIVISION NAME is the official name provided by federal or provincial/territorial authorities
CENSUS SUBDIVISION TYPE - Census subdivisions (CSDs) are classified into 55 types according to official designations adopted by provincial/territorial or federal authorities.
CENSUS SUBDIVISION TYPE DESC contains the full description of the census subdivision type for the record.
CENSUS DIVISION ID - Uniquely identifies a census division (SGC code - composed of the 2-digit province/territory code and the 2-digit census division code).
CENSUS DIVISION NAME - The official census division name.
CENSUS DIVISION TYPE - The type of the census division.
CENSUS DIVISION TYPE DESC contains the full description of the census division type for the record.
CENSUS METRO AREA ID - The CMA/CA code is a three-digit code that uniquely identifies each CMA/CA in Canada.
CENSUS METRO AREA NAME - The official name of the census metropolitan area or census agglomeration.

STAT AREA CLASS TYPE - The Statistical Area Classification (SAC) groups census subdivisions according to whether they are a component of a census metropolitan area, a census agglomeration, or a census metropolitan area or a census agglomeration influenced zone.
STAT AREA CLASS TYPE DESC contains the full description of the statistical area classification type for the record.
ECONOMIC REGION ID - Uniquely identifies an economic region (composed of the 2-digit province/territory code and the 2-digit economic region code).
ECONOMIC REGION NAME - The economic region name.
GEOMETRY is the column used to reference the spatial coordinates defining the feature.

FEATURE_LENGTH_M is the system calculated length or perimeter of a geometry in meters

census-tracts-all-years-.d: The Census Tract Boundary Files portray the census tract boundaries for which Census data are disseminated. Census tracts are small, relatively stable geographic areas that usually have a population of 2,500 to 8,000. They are located in census metropolitan areas and in census agglomerations with an urban core population of 50,000 or more in the previous census. The files contain the boundaries of all 5,076 census tracts located within the 33 census metropolitan areas and 15 census agglomerations which are part of the Census Tract Program. The dataset contains all census years from 2006 to 2016.

coal-ash-chemistry.d: Ash is the inorganic residue remaining after coal combusts. It is composed of oxides of the mineral content in the coal. Coal ash chemistry can have a significant influence on coke strength after reaction (CSR), an important measure of coking coal quality. Coals that were overlain by non-marine deposits (which includes most Canadian Rocky Mountain coals) generally have mineral assemblages that form ashes with low ratios of reactive oxides (i.e. Fe2O3, CaO, MgO, Na2O and K2O) to refractory oxides (i.e. SiO2, Al2O3 and TiO2), which favours good coke strength under blast furnace conditions. Coal ash chemistry is also used to predict slagging and fouling potential in the furnaces or kilns of all types of coals. This database compiles 484 ash chemistry analyses of British Columbia Rocky Mountain bituminous coals from public sources into a standardized relational format to facilitate its distribution and use.

coalfile-database.d: COALFILE documents a collection of 1029 Coal Assessment Reports, which describe exploration and development activity on coal dating from 1990. Many of the reports have been submitted by exploration companies in compliance with the Coal Act. Coal assessment reports have a confidential status for three years from the date of submission. Specific types of information are kept confidential indefinitely; described in detail in Section 2 of the Regulation. The collection also has an additional 196 reports of the Hat Creek area from BC Hydro and the Ministry Library. The information contained in COALFILE is stored as a relational database (MS Access) and includes spatial data for 15,539 boreholes, 546 bulk samples, 3645 trenches, over 5500 maps, and 1924 links to MINFILE. These data are available for download and viewing in MapPlace. All the off-confidential coal assessment reports are downloadable in .pdf with additional digital data as .zip files where available (borehole geophysics, borehole collar information, LiDAR). A search engine leads clients to a summary page for each coal exploration report which describes the data therein and links to the report and data files. The reports, boreholes, bulk samples, and trenches are spatially displayed on MapPlace.
coalfile-database.m: COALFILE began in 1978 as a collection of data from coal assessment reports into a database housed on an IBM Mainframe. In 1992, COALFILE was exported from the IBM Mainframe to the PC as 5 dBASE tables. Since 2003, the database is managed in MS Access.

UNIT TOTAL is the total number of units of all types at the marina. A Unit, typically, is a vacant place in the marina in which boats of different types can be moored.

MOORAGE AVAILABLE indicates whether moorage is available at the marina (Y/N/U).
MAX BOATS is the total number of boats the marina could hold.
AVG DEPTH describes the marina's average water depth in metres.

AVG OCCUPATION provides an indication of the average number of units that have boats moored at any given time during the year. A comparison of the AVG OCCUPATION to the UNIT TOTAL would give a percentage average occupancy for this marina.
PEAK PERIOD indicates the time of year that the marina tends to be most used. i.e. JN-SEPT or SUMMER or ALL YEAR for those marinas that constantly have a high occupancy rate.

GAS AVAILABLE indicates whether gas is available at the marina (Y/N/U).

LUBRICANTS AVAILABLE indicates whether oil/lubricants are available at the marina (Y/N/U).
MARINE SUPPLIES AVAILABLE indicates whether marine supplies are available at the marina (Y/N/U).
POWER AVAILABLE indicates what power amperages are available at the marina (15 / 20 / 30 / 50).
WATER AVAILABLE indicates whether fresh water is available at the marina (Y/N/U).
DISPOSAL AVAILABLE indicates whether garbage disposal is available at the marina (Y/N/U).
WASHROOMS AVAILABLE indicates whether washrooms are available at the marina (Y/N/U).
SHOWERS AVAILABLE indicates whether showers are available at the marina (Y/N/U).
LAUNDRY AVAILABLE indicates whether laundry service is available at the marina (Y/N/U).
RV SITE TOTAL is the total number of recreational vehicle sites at the marina.
LIVE ABOARDS TOTAL is the total number of people who reside onboard their boats while moored at the marina.
HOLDING TANKS TOTAL is the total number of boats that have onboard holding tanks. Holding tanks typically contain liquids such as fresh water or bilge waste.
TREATMENT TYPE is the type of system used by the marina to treat the moored boat's holding tank contents if the holding tanks contain bilge. i.e Sewer, Septic, Dischg
RESTAURANT AVAILABLE indicates whether a restaurant or bar is available at the marina (Y/N/U).
TOURS AVAILABLE indicates whether guided tours are available at the marina (Y/N).
SEASON indicates the range of months that the marina is in operation. i.e. MAY-SEPT

coffee-model-data.d:
The COastal Fall Flood Ensemble Estimation (COFFEE) Model provides a 5-day real-time flow forecasts for select watersheds in coastal British Columbia, including Vancouver Island, South Coast, Central Coast and the North-West. The COFFEE model is updated when a rainfall events occur during the autumn-winter storm season.

Data includes: Water Survey of Canada Gauge Name and Number; station location (latitude/longitude); current stream discharge reading; current flow's annual peak-flow return period; maximum, minimum and average COFFEE model flow forecast over next 5-day period as flow values and relative to annual peak-flow return period estimates.

For detailed information on the COFFEE Model, see the Technical Reference Guide.
coffee-model-data.m: Hydrometric data is published real-time data from the Water Survey of Canada. (Disclaimer for Hydrometric Information and Terms and conditions). Historic data sets from the Water Survey of Canada have been used to analyse return period flows at each location. The COFFEE model utilizes weather forecast information from Environment and Climate Change Canada, and weather observations from Environment and Climate Change Canada, and the Provincial Climate-Related Monitoring Program. Data used in the COFFEE model may be modified from its original values.

community-census-subdivisions.d: BC community place names, associated with their 7-digit CSD codes for a particular census year. Some of these places are incorporated, in which case the community name and the census subdivision name for the associated CSD code will be the same. Others are unincorporated communities with no official boundaries, in which the CSD code is the code for the census subdivision in which the community is located.
fl: Data only as PDF, web pages or images

c: COMMUNITY CENSUS SUBDIV ID is a system generated unique identification number. e.g., 1
COMMUNITY PLACE NAME is name of the community. e.g., 108 Mile House

COMMUNITY PLACE TYPE is the classification of the community. For incorporated communities, this is the census subdivision type desc, e.g., "City", "District Municipality". For unincorporated communities, this is the BCGNIS feature category, e.g., "Unincorporated Rural"

CENSUS YEAR is the census year to which CENSUS SUBDIVISION ID pertains. e.g., 2006, 2011. With CENSUS SUBDIVISION ID, this forms a foreign key linking to CENSUS YEAR + CENSUS SUBDIVISION ID in CEN CENSUS SUBDIVISIONS SP

CENSUS SUBDIVISION ID: With CENSUS YEAR, this forms a foreign Key, linking to CENSUS YEAR + CENSUS SUBDIVISION ID in CEN CENSUS SUBDIVISIONS SP, e.g., 5901022. With CENSUS YEAR, this identifies the census subdivision in which the community is located.
The column used to reference the spatial coordinates defining the feature.
OBJECTID is a column required by spatial layers that interact with ESRI ArcSDE. It is populated with unique values automatically by SDE.

SE_ANNO_CAD_DATA is a binary column used by spatial tools to store annotation, curve features and CAD
data when using the SDO_GEOMETRY storage data type.

community-health-service-areas-boundarie.d:
Community Health Service Area (CHSA) boundaries; 2022 boundary configuration.

The CHSAs are a mutually exclusive and exhaustive classification of the land area in BC. CHSAs are contiguous (land area is geographically adjacent) and fit within the existing geographical hierarchy (cannot violate higher-level geography boundaries such as the Local Health Area).
community-health-service-areas-boundarie.m:
CHSA boundaries are based on Statistics Canada Census geographies, with the census Dissemination Block used as the foundation, and in 2022 were revised to correspond with 2021 Census boundaries. The revised CHSA boundaries have been implemented as of April 1, 2023.

CHSAs were originally implemented in April 2019.

consolidated-local-health-areas-boundari.d:
Consolidated Local Health Areas (CLHAs) Boundaries.

B.C. Consolidated Local Health Areas (CLHAs) are a health geography standard that partitions the province into distinct areas that support coordination of specialized care between Health Authorities and Primary Care. The province is divided into five Health Authorities, which are subdivided into 41 Consolidated Local Health Areas (CLHAs), which are subdivided into 231 Community Health Service Areas (CHSAs).

CLHAs encompass all of B.C., so the classification is exhaustive of all the land area in the province.
consolidated-local-health-areas-boundari.m: Every five years Statistics Canada performs a census (next one in 2026). After the census is complete MoH is anticipated to update their CHSA boundaries. CLHAs are groupings of CHSAs so any updates to CHSA boundaries may result in updates to CLHA boundaries. Otherwise there are no anticipated changes to CLHAs.

consolidated-wetlands-points.d:
The Consolidated Wetlands – Points layer was created to improve access and understanding of available wetland spatial data in British Columbia (BC), Canada. This dataset brings together identified wetlands, and wetland attributes, from multiple sources improving access to wetland data and reducing duplication of effort to compile and interpret wetland data. The creation of the Consolidated Wetlands - Points layer included the identification, acquisition, evaluation, and consolidation of wetland spatial data sources into a single harmonized schema.

This data is a result of a project initiated under the 5-year Nature Smart Climate Solutions contribution agreement between Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) and the BC Ministry of Water, Land and Resource Stewardship (WLRS) titled *BC Wetlands Inventory, Policy and Education*.

count-of-civil-suits-initiated-by-fiscal.d: Under the Civil Forfeiture Act, the director (Minister or delegate) may apply to the court for an order forfeiting to the government, (a) the whole of an interest in property that is proceeds of unlawful activity, or (b) the portion of an interest in property that is proceeds of unlawful activity. The director may also apply to the court for an order forfeiting to the government property that is an instrument of unlawful activity. counties-of-british-columbia-legally-def.d:
The Counties of British Columbia contains areas of land within the Province of British Columbia representing legally defined administrative areas described in the County Boundary Act. The purpose of this division is for the administration of justice.

The counties were delineated using provincial base mapping features, following the metes and bounds descriptions in the Letters Patent.

A polygon dataset that includes all of the administrative areas currently in the Administrative Boundaries Management System (ABMS) is available here (https://catalogue.data.gov.bc.ca/dataset/legally-defined-administrative-areas-of-bc).

A complimentary point dataset that defines the administrative areas is also available here (https://catalogue.data.gov.bc.ca/dataset/legally-defined-administrative-areas-of-bc-boundary-locations).

The Legal document which divides the province of British Columbia into counties is available here (http://www.bclaws.ca/civix/document/id/complete/statreg/96075_01).

Other individual datasets are available from the following …

Other sources were used to clarify boundaries (e.g., Tantalis for crown land parcels, legal plans, etc.).

country-trade-app-data.d:
Data published to the BC Stats Country Trade application: https://bcstats.shinyapps.io/CountryTradeApp/.

For immigration data, all values between 0 and 5 are shown as “0”. This is done to prevent individuals from being identified when IRCC data is compiled and compared to other publicly available statistics. All other values are rounded to the closest multiple of 5 for the same reason.

Data from the International Trade Centre is rounded to the nearest trillion.

Investment data that is suppressed or unavailable for a specific time period will appear as zero.

If you need help with this dataset, you can reach BC Stats at the email below; however, submitting a support request is recommended.

Data sourced from Statistics Canada, the International Monetary Fund (IMF), the International Trade Centre (ITC), Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC), the United States Census Bureau, Bureau of Economic Analysis (U.S.), and the International Trade Administration (U.S. Department of Commerce), and is current as of February 23, 2026.

court-findings-on-completed-prosecutions.m: The Justice Information System (JUSTIN) is an itegrated case management system which means that information about each case is entered only once, and is re-used by various justice agencies as the case moves from initiation through to disposition. courts-annual-report-10-yr-comparison-.d:
---

This is a 10 Year Report by court level, division and class, as represented by the Court Services Branch.

• “Session Hours” refers to the amount of time a matter is heard in court.

• “Scheduled Court Appearances” refers to the number of occasions when cases are scheduled to be before the court for a specific reason, such as the first appearance, case conference, trial, and sentencing. (* Note that not all scheduled appearances occur, and they may be adjourned prior to the appearance date).

• “New Court Cases” generally refers to the number of new filings received in a court location that initiate a case, including files transferred from another registry for disposition.

• “Concluded Cases” indicates the number of Provincial Court criminal cases with a final disposition recorded against all charges on an Information or ticket.

• Fiscal Year datasets are available and are based on when the matter was heard.

critical-habitat-for-federally-listed-sp.d:
This dataset displays the geographic areas within which critical habitat for species at risk listed on Schedule 1 of the federal Species at Risk Act (SARA) occurs in British Columbia. However, not all of the area within these boundaries is necessarily critical habitat. To precisely define what constitutes critical habitat for a particular species it is essential that this geospatial information be considered in conjunction with complementary information in a species’ recovery document. Recovery documents are available from the Species at Risk (SAR) Public Registry (https://www.canada.ca/en/environment-climate-change/services/species-risk-public-registry.html). The recovery documents contain important information about the interpretation of the geospatial information, especially regarding the biological and environmental features (“biophysical attributes”) that complete the definition of a species’ critical habitat.

This dataset includes both “final” critical habitat, and “proposed” critical habitat within British Columbia, as it is depicted in the recovery documents. “Proposed” critical habitat depicted in proposed recovery documents has not been formally identified and is subject to change before it is posted as final. Despite the use of the term “final”, it is important to note that recovery documents (and therefore critical habitat) may be amended from time to time. Species are added as the data becomes ready, which may occur after the recovery document has been posted …

files.n: Critical Habitat for federally-listed species at risk - tabular summary

c: CRITICAL_HABITAT_ID: is a system generated unique identification number. This is the primary key of this table. e.g., 1

COSEWIC_SPECIES_ID is a unique identification number assigned to the species or taxa (including, if applicable, sub species and population) assessed by the Committee on the Status of Endangered Wildlife in Canada (COSEWIC) and currently listed on SARA Schedule 1; e.g., '1086'.
SCIENTIFIC_NAME is the standard scientific name for the SARA-listed species or taxa, and can include subspecies; e.g., 'Oreoscoptes montanus'.
COMMON_NAME_ENGLISH is the English name of the species or taxa listed on SARA Schedule 1; e.g., 'Sage Thrasher'.
COMMON_NAME_FRENCH is the French name of the species or taxa listed on SARA Schedule 1; e.g., 'Moqueur des armoises'.

COSEWIC_POPULATION is the population name of the species or taxa assessed by the Committee on the Status of Endangered Wildlife in Canada (COSEWIC) and currently listed on SARA Schedule 1; e.g., 'Southern Mountain population'.
CRITICAL_HABITAT_STATUS is the stage of development of the critical habitat polygon; e.g., 'Final' or 'Candidate'
CRITICAL_HABITAT_REGION is a regional identifier optionally used to group critical habitat polygons; e.g. "Southeastern BC".
CRITICAL_HABITAT_SITE_ID is the alphanumeric code of a critical habitat site as defined in the federal recovery document; e.g., '937_5'.
CRITICAL_HABITAT_SITE_NAME is the name of a critical habitat site as defined in the federal recovery document; e.g., 'Kilpoola'.

CRITICAL_HABITAT_DETAIL is the level of detail of critical habitat polygon; e.g., 'Detailed polygon' or 'Grid square'. Grid squares are used when detailed polygons contain sensitive information that cannot be released.
CRITICAL_HABITAT_VARIANT is the sub-type of critical habitat, if applicable; e.g. 'Regeneration'.
CRITICAL_HABITAT_APPROACH is the scale at which the polygons were defined and refers to processes within the Critical Habitat Toolbox policy; e.g., 'Landscape', 'Area' or 'Site'.
CRITICAL_HABITAT_METHOD is a broad description of how the critical habitat was identified and refers to processes within the Critical Habitat Toolbox policy; e.g., 'Critical Function Zone'.
AREA_HECTARES is the area calculated in hectares at source data which is in Lambert Conic Conformal. E.g., 14430833.7926
LAND_TENURE is the status of federal crown ownership of the land; e.g., 'Federal' or 'Non-federal'.
CRITICAL_HABITAT_COMMENTS are notes about the critical habitat or specific polygon; e.g., 'Polygons were identified as part of a multispecies recovery plan'.
CRITICAL_HABITAT_DATE_EDITED is the date that the polygon was last edited; e.g., '8/21/2014'.
PROVINCE_TERRITORY is the province or territory in which the critical habitat occurs; e.g., 'British Columbia'.

FEDERAL_DEPARTMENT_NAME is the Federal department or agency that published the recovery strategy or action plan in which the critical habitat is identified, and maintains the data; e.g., 'Canadian Wildlife Service', ‘Parks Canada Agency’.

UTM_ZONE is a segment of the Earth's surface 6 degrees of longitude in width. The zones are numbered eastward starting at the meridian 180 degrees from the prime meridian at Greenwich. There are five zones numbered 7 through 11 that cover British Columbia, e.g., Zone 10 with a central meridian at …
UTM EASTING is the distance in meters of the polygon centroid eastward to or from the central meridian of a UTM zone with a false easting of 500000 meters. E.g., 532538
UTM NORTHING is the distance in meters of the polygon centroidnorthward from the equator. e.g., 5747966
LATITUDE is the geographic coordinate, in decimal degrees (dd.dddddd), of the location of the feature as measured from the equator, e.g., 55.323653
LONGITUDE is the geographic coordinate, in decimal degrees (ddd.dddddd), of the location of the feature as measured from the prime meridian, e.g., -123.093544
SHAPE is the column used to reference the spatial coordinates defining the feature.
OBJECTID is a column required by spatial layers that interact with ESRI ArcSDE. It is populated with unique values automatically by SDE.
SE ANNO CAD DATA is a binary column used by spatial tools to store annotation, curve features and CAD data when using the SDO_GEOMETRY storage data type.

crown-charge-assessment-decisions.d: A count of the charge assessment decisions made by the BC Prosecution Service.
crown-charge-assessment-decisions.m: The Justice Information System (JUSTIN) is an itegrated case management system which means that information about each case is entered only once, and is re-used by various justice agencies as the case moves from initiation through to disposition. JUSTIN supports the core business functions in criminal case processing and is used by RCMP, municipal police, Crown Counsel and Criminal Courts registry staff, Sheriff, Probation Services, Victim/Witness Services, Trial Schedulers, Judicial Case Managers and Corrections staff and some other Justice System partners.

crown-contaminated-sites.d: This data set represents general site location points where the Crown Contaminated Sites Program (CCSP) has conducted work from 2022 to 2024. The work is outlined in the 2024 Biennial Report which documents progress over the past two years. CCSP work includes investigating, remediating, and monitoring prioritized, high risk Crown contaminated sites resulting from historical industrial (mining) activities where responsibility has defaulted to, or has been accepted by, the Crown. For further information, please review the Biennial Report posted on the Crown Contaminated Sites Program web page or Story Map (https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content?id=1994A20106B1490B8C470996F60A83C5).
crown-contaminated-sites.m: The Crown Contaminated Sites Program produces a Biennial Report. The data for the Crown Contaminates Sites will therefore be updated every 2 years.

current-census-consolidated-subdivisions.d:
A census consolidated subdivision (CCS) is a statistical area of aggregated census subdivisions used by the Census of Agriculture. A census consolidated subdivision is a grouping of adjacent census subdivisions. Generally, the smaller more urban census subdivisions (towns, villages, etc.) are combined with the surrounding, larger, more rural census subdivision, in order to create a geographic level between the census subdivision and the census division. The dataset is for census year 2016.

Source: Statistics Canada, Census consolidated subdivisions, 2016. Reproduced and distributed on an "as is" basis with the permission of Statistics Canada.

current-census-metropolitan-areas.d:
A census metropolitan area (CMA) or a census agglomeration (CA) is formed by one or more adjacent municipalities centred on a large urban area (known as the urban core). The census population count of the urban core is at least 10,000 to form a census agglomeration and at least 50,000 to form a census metropolitan area.

Source: Statistics Canada, Census metropolitan areas and census agglomerations, 2016. Reproduced and distributed on an "as is" basis with the permission of Statistics Canada.

The Census Tract Boundary Files portray the census tract boundaries for which 2006 Census data are disseminated. Census tracts are small, relatively stable geographic areas that usually have a population of 2,500 to 8,000. They are located in census metropolitan areas and in census agglomerations with an urban core population of 50,000 or more in the previous census. The files contain the boundaries of all 5,076 census tracts located within the 33 census metropolitan areas and 15 census agglomerations which are part of the Census Tract Program.

Source: Statistics Canada, Census tracts, 2016. Reproduced and distributed on an "as is" basis with the permission of Statistics Canada.

current-season-automated-snow-weather-st.d:
The British Columbia Automated Snow Weather Station Network (http://bcrfc.env.gov.bc.ca/data/asp/index.htm) comprises monitoring stations operated by the Ministry of Environment, BC Hydro, Rio Tinto Alcan, the Greater Vancouver Water District and many other partner organizations. There are Automated Snow Weather Stations (ASWS) (http://bcrfc.env.gov.bc.ca/about/snow-pillow.htm) monitoring sites around the province, mostly in remote and high elevation locations. Station location data are available here (https://catalogue.data.gov.bc.ca/dataset/ebe546aa-ac34-491c-a828-fdc87fb70610). Data is collected hourly and transmitted through the GOES satellites. Remotely sensed snow and meteorological data (snow water equivalent in mm, snow depth in cm, air temperature in degrees Celcius, cumulative precipitation in mm) from ASWS stations are available in near real-time. The current year ASWS data are updated hourly, combining the data for the current water year (October 1st to September 30th) for all active ASWS stations in the province.

Data can be directly accessed via the Real-Time Water tool (https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content?id=39A675506AE54C4CB240849338B7C8D8) and the Snow Stations Interactive Map (https://governmentofbc.maps.arcgis.com/apps/webappviewer/index.html?id=c15768bf73494f5da04b1aac6793bd2e).

current-season-manual-snow-survey-data.d:
This data file contains the current year (December to April) snow pack level manual observations from across British Columbia. Manual snow survey sites are actively surveyed as part of the BC Snow Survey program (http://bcrfc.env.gov.bc.ca/). Manual snow surveys are conducted up to eight times per year around the beginning of every month from January through June with extra measurements at mid-month in May and June. Active and inactive snow course locations are available here (https://catalogue.data.gov.bc.ca/dataset/9f653102-5627-45a7-bd4c-686e365ee04a). The majority of snow courses are located between 1000 and 2000 metres above sea level. Five or ten location points within a sampling area are chosen and referenced to trees etc. which will be visible when there is snow on the ground. At each sampling period, measurements are made at all of the location points at the sampling site -- the data point for that site is the average snow depth (cm) and water equivalent (mm) of the measured location points. Other attributes in the data set include: site number, survey period, elevation (m) and percent of normal. Archived snow pack level manual observations are available here (https://catalogue.data.gov.bc.ca/dataset/705df46f-e9d6-4124-bc4a-66f54c07b228).

Data can be directly accessed via the Real-Time Water tool (https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content?id=39A675506AE54C4CB240849338B7C8D8) and the Snow Stations Interactive Map …

The dataset is updated on a Daily basis to incorporate newly reported incidents and updates to existing records.

This number comprises 20 executive users, 93 data professionals and 154 business users from 24 ministries and associated public agencies. This calculates the number of housing units that reflect additional demand for housing, beyond the minimum units required to adequately house current and anticipated residents. disaster-response-routes.d:
Critical Routes are identified pre-disaster to purposefully develop key routes for resilience planning, and to categorize transportation infrastructure to purposefully plan that there will be key routes available, at minimum, for emergency responders and emergency resources immediately after a disaster. Critical routes include a combination of municipal, provincial, and federal infrastructure and are the primary corridors of movement in an impact area.

During a disaster, Critical Routes may be designated as Disaster Response Routes (DRRs) to temporarily prioritize the movement of people and/or goods to achieve emergency response objectives. DRRs may or may not coincide with critical routes, may be multi-modal, and could change due to the circumstances to address the immediate need. DRRs are flexible and adaptable to a particular event for distinct movement of resources. DRRs may only be capable of supporting emergency responder vehicles. DRRs are not automatically activated because they must be coordinated. These routes are regulated by the Ministry of Transportation and Transit.

drinking-water-sources-intakes-wellheads.d:
Point features showing the location of intakes and/or wellheads for drinking water systems. A drinking water system is any domestic system servicing anything other than a single-family dwelling, as defined in the Drinking Water Protection Act. These locations are updated as more information is received and is therefore continually being updated and may or may not match the corresponding Point of Diversion locations available through the Water Rights dataset and application.

This is one of three Drinking Water Sources datasets (along with the DWS - Source Areas polygons dataset, and DWS - Protection Zones polygons dataset). Note: the polygons all have unique polygon IDs used to relate them to these points.
drinking-water-sources-intakes-wellheads.m: Data was provided by each Provincial Health Authority in 2024, which was cleaned and back-filled using the Water Rights Licenses dataset and the Groundwater Wells dataset. Only data that could be verified and locations that were deemed accurate were included in the first draft. Data clean-up priorities are underway to continue to clean and validate this data with the intention of continuing to add new data to the dataset.

drinking-water-sources-protection-zones.d:
Polygon features showing various zones of protection around drinking water system intakes/wellheads. A drinking water system is any domestic system servicing anything other than a single-family dwelling, as defined in the Drinking Water Protection Act. Zone of protection is a broad term that represents a wide variety of areas as they have been delineated in their corresponding report. The methods and processes used to delineate these zones vary based on several factors including, but not limited to, population, vulnerability, hydrologic/hydrogeologic parameters, etc.
For the use of this dataset, the term Protection Zone means that protection measures should be considered and/or implemented in these areas due to the importance of these areas supplying drinking water to their water system users. Protection Zone does not mean that protection measures have been implemented in these areas, nor that protection measures are not required beyond the boundary of these areas.

This is one of three Drinking Water Sources datasets (along with the DWS - Intakes/Wellheads points dataset, and DWS - Source Areas polygons dataset). Note: these polygons have unique Protection Zone IDs used to relate them to the Intakes/Wellhead points.

drinking-water-sources-source-areas.d:
Polygon features representing the geographical extent of a source area that contributes water to a drinking water system. A drinking water system is any domestic system servicing anything other than a single-family dwelling, as defined in the Drinking Water Protection Act. Source Area is a broad term used to describe any area that could potentially contribute water to the drinking water system; it does not mean that hydrologic analyses have been completed to determine likelihood of connectivity. These source areas most often represent the entire aquifer extent (for ground water systems) or the watershed upstream from the intake (for surface water systems).

This is one of three Drinking Water Sources datasets (along with the DWS - Intakes/Wellheads points dataset, and DWS - Protection Zones polygons dataset). Note: these polygons have unique Source Areas IDs used to relate them to the Intakes/Wellhead points.
drinking-water-sources-source-areas.m: As new intake and wellhead points are added to the Drinking Water Sources - Intakes/Wellheads dataset, source areas are generated. Source areas for surface water intakes (i.e., contributing watersheds) are delineated in-house and added to this dataset continually. Source areas for wellheads (i.e., aquifer boundary) are auto-pulled from the Ground Water Aquifers dataset using the Well Tag Number and correlated Aquifer ID as it exists in the GWELLS Application.

drought-aquatic-ecosystem-monitoring-loc.d:
These layers display data on aquatic ecosystem risks and impacts for regional priority watersheds and locations.

Drought conditions are typically monitored following spring freshet (the seasonal rise in water levels resulting from melting snowpack) until the onset of winter conditions. This timing can vary considerably for different areas of the province from year to year depending on conditions. When drought conditions are actively monitored, drought levels are typically set weekly or biweekly.

To learn more about drought conditions, patterns and trends visit the B.C. Drought Information Portal (https://droughtportal.gov.bc.ca/).

Ecological Aquatic Units of British Columbia (EAU BC) is a hierarchical classification
of BC's freshwater ecosystems. EAU BC classifies freshwater systems at
three spatial scales - Freshwater Ecoregions, Ecological Drainage Units, and River and Lake Ecosystems - based on measurable environmental features, processes and biological data. Freshwater Ecoregions are defined based on zoogeographic patterns in fish recolonization following the last glacial recession. Five Freshwater Ecoregions are identified in BC.

tg: Ecological Aquatic Units of British Columbia
eaubc-lakes.d: River and Lake Ecosystem Types nest within both Ecological Drainage Units and Freshwater Ecoregions. They are therefore defined by zoogeographic, physiographic and climatic patterns but also take into account more localized physical habitat and dominant environmental processes that shape freshwater ecosystems. The units of analysis for lake ecosystems in BC are at a scale of 1:50,000. Biological information is sparse at this scale of the classification and is therefore not explicitly used to delineate ecosystem types. However, fish assemblages can be inferred for each Ecosystem Type based on the Ecological Drainage Unit it is nested within. Twelve Lake Ecosystem Types are identified in BC.

Note: Data not available yet. We expect data to be loaded 2025/2026
The B.C. Conservation Data Centre's (CDC) spatial range layer is a broad-scale representation of an ecological community's geographic distribution in British Columbia. The data are created using Biogeoclimatic Ecosystem Classification (BEC) polygons. The ecological community ranges are split up by 1:50,000 National Topographic Map (NTS) sheets in order to improve performance of the dataset. Range data generally exist for ecological communities that are at-risk in BC (i.e. red-listed and blue-listed), but may be limited by the availability of accurate distribution data. New ecological community ranges will be added to this dataset periodically, and existing ranges will be updated as additional information becomes available.

edva-conversion-tables.d:
These tables provide the conversion of voting areas (VAs) updated as a result of a provincial redistribution.

Each voting area is shown with the three character electoral district code followed by the numeric voting area code (e.g. CHC009 is voting area 009 in the Chilliwack electoral district).

The VA conversions are provided for the province as a whole, together with a separate worksheet for each ED indicated by the ED’s code (e.g. ABM for Abbotsford-Mission) on the worksheet tab. There may be more than one VA geographically associated with each VA.
edva-conversion-tables.m: Electoral Geography Division, Elections BC. Converted from Informix/DB2 to Microsoft excel files by Elections BC.

eelgrasses-coastal-resource-information-.d: Distribution of eelgrasses in coastal British Columbia showing relative abundance (RA) and overall relative importance (RI). RI is based on project region and not on the province as a whole. CRIMS is a legacy dataset of BC coastal resource data that was acquired in a systematic and synoptic manner from 1979 and was intermittently updated throughout the years. Resource information was collected in nine study areas using a peer-reviewed provincial Resource Information Standards Committee consisting of DFO Fishery Officers, First Nations, and other subject matter experts. There are currently no plans to update this legacy data.

electoral-areas-legally-defined-administ.d:
Legally defined Electoral Area polygons were drawn from metes and bounds descriptions as written in Letters Patent for Regional District Electoral Areas in the province of British Columbia. In the event of a discrepancy in the data, the metes and bounds description will prevail.

Although the boundaries were drawn based on the legal metes and bounds descriptions, they may differ from how regional districts and their member municipalities and electoral areas currently view and/or manage their boundaries. Where discrepancies are noted, the Ministry of Housing and Municipal Affairs (the custodian) enters into discussion with the local governments whose boundaries are affected. In order to effect a change to the boundary, Cabinet approval is required. This is done through an Order in Council (OIC). While discrepancies to administrative boundaries are being resolved, boundaries may be adjusted on an ongoing basis until the requested changes are completed.

The OIC_YEAR and OIC_NUMBER fields indicate the year that the boundary was passed under OIC and its associated number. The AFFECTED_ADMIN_AREA_ABRVN identifies the administrative areas that are affected by the OIC.

A polygon dataset that includes all of the administrative areas currently in the Administrative Boundaries Management System (ABMS) is available here (https://catalogue.data.gov.bc.ca/dataset/legally-defined-administrative-areas-of-bc).

A complimentary point dataset that defines the administrative areas is also …

Other sources were used to clarify boundaries (e.g., Tantalis for crown land parcels, legal plans, etc.).

electoral-district-voting-area-to-munici.d:
This dataset contains a conversion table of provincial electoral district voting areas and local government administrative areas in British Columbia.

A voting area is a defined geographic area within an electoral district. Voting areas are assigned to voting places in order to facilitate the administration of elections. (Election Act, s. 1, 80)

When creating voting area boundaries Elections BC tries to follow municipal boundaries, but in some cases, voting areas will split a municipal boundary to satisfy administrative requirements.

There are two tables attached to this record.

A conversion table of voting areas that were gazetted on 2017/02/23 and were used in the 2017 Provincial General Election, the 2018 Kelowna West By-Election, 2019 Nanaimo By-Election, the 2020 Provincial General Election, the 2022 Vancouver-Quilchena and Surrey South By-Elections, and the 2023 Vancouver-Mount Pleasant and Langford-Juan de Fuca By-Elections.

A conversion table of voting areas that were gazetted on 2024/09/19 that will be used for the 2024 Provincial General Election scheduled for October 19, 2024.
electoral-district-voting-area-to-munici.m:
Report generated by the Electoral Geography division at Elections BC using GIS software, based on overlay of provincial electoral district voting areas and municipal boundaries.

This dataset is updated on an ongoing basis as municipal and provincial electoral district voting area boundaries change.

electrical-logs-elogs-of-the-shallow-sub.d: These elogs provide information about the shallow and mostly unconsolidated materials overlying bedrock in the Peace River region of northeastern British Columbia. They can be used to interpret depth to bedrock, possible water bearing intervals, lithology and other aspects of the shallow subsurface.
electrical-logs-elogs-of-the-shallow-sub.m: The elogs are scanned from hardcopies stored on the 6th floor of 1810 Blanshard St in Victoria. They comprise portions of exploration reports submitted to the government to fulfill the work requirements of exploration permits.

elf-model-data.d:
The Extrapolating Logarithmic Flow (ELF) Model is an empirical mathematical model for estimating a 30-day stream flow forecast during the summer low flow season at Water Survey of Canada hydrometric gauge locations in British Columbia.

This map provides mapped flow forecast output from the ELF model against assessed mean annual discharge and mean annual gauge level at Water Survey of Canada locations.

Data includes: Water Survey of Canada Gauge Name and Number; station location (latitude/longitude); analysed station mean annual discharge; analysed station mean annual gauge height; minimum recorded gauge level; current discharge; percentage of current discharge to mean annual discharge; current gauge height; percentage of current gauge height to mean annual gauge level; ELF Model minimum, maximum and average forecasted flow over following 30-day period; ELF Model minimum, maximum and average forecasted flow as percentage of mean annual discharge over following 30-day period; ELF Model minimum, maximum and average forecasted gauge level over following 30-day period; ELF Model minimum, maximum and average forecasted gauge level as percentage of mean annual gauge level over following 30-day period; time of update of data.
elf-model-data.m: Hydrometric data is published real-time data from the Water Survey of Canada. (Disclaimer for Hydrometric Information and Terms and conditions). Historic data sets from the Water Survey of Canada have been used to analyse return period flows at each location. Data used in the ELF model may be modified from its original values.

elk-valley-water-quality-plan.d:
The Elk Valley Area Based Management Plan (ABMP) - “Elk Valley Water Quality Plan” was developed according to Ministerial Order No. 113 to remediate water quality effects of past coal mining and to guide future development.

The Elk Valley Water Quality Plan was developed by Teck with input from the public, First Nations, governments, technical experts and other stakeholders. The purpose of the Plan is to identify a strategy and implement solutions to address increasing selenium and nitrate water concentrations within the Valley, and assess and track levels of cadmium and sulphate in waters; while at the same time allowing for continued sustainable mining in the Valley. The Plan also lays out a strategy to address calcite formation associated with historical and current mining activity.

The Plan was submitted to the British Columbia Minister of Environment for approval on July 22, 2014. The ministry amended the Elk Valley ABMP in 2025. More information can be found at https://elkvalleywaterquality.gov.bc.ca/.

environmental-monitoring-data-system-enm.d:
Environmental monitoring locations from the Environmental Monitoring Data System (EnMoDS) (https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content?id=BDE7F9F4BC4546629582CEBC4ABC8101).

These point location records show where discrete environmental monitoring may have taken place. Locations are generally in naturalized settings such as rivers and lakes, but also include anthropogenic features like wells and industrial facilities including waste discharges. Key attribute fields for filtering include, location ID, location type, location group, observation count, and most recent field visit date.

Observational results for each location can be accessed from EnMoDS Web Reporting (https://enmodswr.nrs.gov.bc.ca/) or from EnMoDS Results Data Records (https://catalogue.data.gov.bc.ca/dataset/83a585fe-effb-48bd-8a03-d35db4eeb1bb).

Information regarding changes from the Environmental Monitoring System along with other resources are available on the EnMoDS website listed in related links below.

evacuation-orders-and-alerts.d:
During a declared emergency event, this file represents an aggregated dataset that shows all of the active Orders and Alerts in the Province as initiated by the Local Governments or First Nations.

When an Order or Alert is rescinded, its status changes to All Clear. The polygon is removed from this layer and copied to the Historical Orders and Alerts dataset (https://catalogue.data.gov.bc.ca/dataset/historical-orders-and-alerts).

Data updates are loaded to the BC Geographic Warehouse at 10 minutes past every hour. During periods of active emergency events, replications may be made more frequently.

Dec 19, 2018: The model has been updated so that areas under the same order or alert are combined to display as a single area.

fire-burn-severity-historical.d:
This layer is the one-year-later burn severity classification for large fires (greater than 100 ha). Burn severity mapping is conducted using best available pre- and post-fire satellite multispectral imagery acquired by the MultiSpectral Instrument (MSI) aboard the Sentinel-2 satellite or the Operational Land Imager (OLI) sensor aboard the Landsat-8 and 9 satellites. The post-fire imagery is acquired during the subsequent growing season. Mapping conducted during the subsequent growing season benefits from greater post-fire image availability and is expected to be more representative of tree mortality. Every attempt is made to use cloud, smoke, shadow and snow-free imagery that was acquired prior to September 30th.

Please note, this layer is 1-year-later burn severity dataset. The same-year burn severity mapping dataset (WHSE_FOREST_VEGETATION.VEG_BURN_SEVERITY_SAME_YR_SP) is considered an interim product to this layer.

#### Methodology:

• Select suitable pre- and post-fire imagery or create a cloud/snow/smoke-free composite from multiple images scenes

• Calculate normalized burn severity ratio (NBR) for pre- and post-fire images

• Calculate difference NBR (dNBR) where dNBR = pre NBR – post NBR

• Apply a scaling equation (dNBR_scaled = dNBR*1000 + 275)/5)

• Apply BARC thresholds (76, 110, 187) to create a 4-class image (unburned, low severity, medium severity, and high severity)

• Apply region-based filters to reduce noise

• Confirm burn severity analysis results …

fire-burn-severity-same-year.d:
This layer is the current fire year burn severity classification for large fires (greater than 100 ha). Burn severity mapping is conducted using best available pre- and post-fire satellite multispectral imagery acquired by the MultiSpectral Instrument (MSI) aboard the Sentinel-2 satellite or the Operational Land Imager (OLI) sensor aboard the Landsat-8 and 9 satellites. Every attempt is made to use cloud, smoke, shadow and snow-free imagery that was acquired prior to September 30th. However, in late fire seasons imagery acquired after September 30th may be used.

This layer is considered an interim product for the 1-year-later burn severity dataset (WHSE_FOREST_VEGETATION.VEG_BURN_SEVERITY_SP). Mapping conducted during the following growing season benefits from greater post-fire image availability and is expected to be more representative of tree mortality.

#### Methodology:

• Select suitable pre- and post-fire imagery or create a cloud/snow/smoke-free composite from multiple images scenes

• Calculate normalized burn severity ratio (NBR) for pre- and post-fire images

• Calculate difference NBR (dNBR) where dNBR = pre NBR – post NBR

• Apply a scaling equation (dNBR_scaled = dNBR*1000 + 275)/5)

• Apply BARC thresholds (76, 110, 187) to create a 4-class image (unburned, low severity, medium severity, and high severity)

• Mask out water bodies using a satellite-derived water layer

• Apply region-based filters to reduce noise

• Confirm burn severity analysis results …

Locations are based on the location of the main community, as obtained from Aboriginal Affairs and Northern Development Canada (AANDC). This data includes 6 Yukon or NWT bands that have parts of their traditional territories in B.C. and have been accepted into the BC treaty process. This is a multipoint feature. fish-holding-areas-coastal-resource-info.d: Fish holding areas (i.e. areas of concentration of salmon and herring, both adult and juvenile) in coastal British Columbia. Attribute information includes overall relative importance, species of salmon and other fish observed at various times throughout the year as well as information on spawning activity and larvae. CRIMS is a legacy dataset of BC coastal resource data that was acquired in a systematic and synoptic manner from 1979 and was intermittently updated throughout the years. Resource information was collected in nine study areas using a peer-reviewed provincial Resource Information Standards Committee consisting of DFO Fishery Officers, First Nations, and other subject matter experts. There are currently no plans to update this legacy data.

flood-advisory-and-warning-notification-.d:
Map-based product of current Flood Warnings and Advisories issued by the River Forecast Centre.

The map includes the spatial extent of areas, such as regions or specific watersheds, that are under advisory/warning, with links to text version of the warning/advisory with greater detail.

Levels of Warnings/Advisories: 1. High Streamflow Advisory: River levels are rising or expected to rise rapidly, but that no major flooding is expected. Minor flooding in low-lying areas is possible. 2. Flood Watch: River levels are rising and will approach or may exceed bankfull. Flooding of areas adjacent to affected rivers may occur. 3. Flood Warning: River levels have exceeded bankfull or will exceed bankfull imminently, and that flooding of areas adjacent to the rivers affected will result.
flood-advisory-and-warning-notification-.m: Advisories and warnings are issued by the River Forecast Centre based on interpretation and evaluation of streamflow data, weather data, weather forecasts, hydrologic modelling and hydrologic analysis.

forest-drought-risk-assessment-tool.d:
Forest Drought Risk Assessment Tool (ForDRAT) provides estimates of stand-level drought risk for various BC
tree species (Interior only at this point). Drought risk estimates are provided across different biogeoclimatic units and relative soil moisture regimes for both current and future climates.

The data are currently provided in a spreadsheet, with the following columns:
1. BGC: Biogeoclimatic zone, subzone and variant.
2. Period: Data are provided for three historical periods: (i) 1961-1990 climate normal period; (ii) 1971-2000; and (iii) 1981-2010.
Projected drought risk is provided for three future periods: (i) 2020 (2011-2040); (ii) 2050 (2041-2070); and (iii) 2080 (2071-2100).
3. SMR_text: Text description of relative soil moisture regime.
4. SMR: Integer code of relative soil moisture regime.
5. AET_PET: Mean annual ratio of actual to potential
evapotranspiration.
6. The remaining columns provide estimated drought risk by species. Species codes are as follows: (i) Pl = lodgepole pine; (ii) Sx = hybrid white spruce; (iii) Fd = Douglas-fir (interior variety); (iv) Bl = subalpine fir; (v) Cw = western redcedar; (vi) Hw = western hemlock; (vii) Lw = western larch; (viii) Py = ponderosa pine; (ix) Ac = black cottonwood; and (x) At = trembling aspen. More species will be added over time.

Details on ForDRAT development are provided in the following resources:

forest-harvesting-restrictions-generaliz.d:
Spatial representation of various land designations that stipulate, to varying degrees, limits on forest harvesting activity. These land designations include, for example, parks, ecological reserves, conservancies, ungulate winter ranges, wildlife management areas, old growth management areas, visual quality objective areas.

This spatial representation should be used only for strategic-level analysis and may not represent the most up-to-date or all land designations that have provisions that limit forest harvesting activity. The areas captured in this layer are not the authoritative legal representation of the land designations.

The 'Ranking of Forest Harvesting Restrictions' resource describes the various land designations and how they are ranked. The ranking influences which land designation will take precedence when multiple land designations spatially overlap. This is one reason why Generalized Forest Harvesting Restrictions spatial data is not the authoritative legal representation of the land designations -because parts of lower ranked land designations may be missing if they are overlapped by higher ranked land designations.

For example, an "Old Growth Management Area (OGMA): Legal" has a higher rank than a "Ungulate Winter Range: Conditional harvest". In cases where an "Old Growth Management Area (OGMA): Legal" spatially overlaps an "Ungulate Winter Range: Conditional harvest", only the "Old Growth Management Area (OGMA): Legal" is portrayed in the Generalized …
