forest-inventory-ground-plot-data-and-in.d:
The 'Data and Resources' box to the right includes a link to an FTP site where data, and a data dictionary, can be downloaded that provide access to compiled data from the primary ground-sampling programs managed by the Forest Analysis and Inventory Branch (FAIB) as well as a link to and Interactive Mapping App.

FAIB ground-sampling programs include the Permanent Sample Plots (PSPs) that provide long term growth and yield information to support development and testing of growth-and-yield models. Active PSPs are the only plot type protected from harvesting. The Provincial Change Monitoring Inventory (CMI), Provincial Young Stand Monitoring (YSM) and National Forest Inventory (NFI) programs monitor the changes in growth, mortality, and forest health from statistically valid populations. Vegetation Resource Inventory (VRI) plots are used to audit and verify key spatial inventory attributes estimated during photo interpretation.

The 'Ground Plot Data FTP' link contains tree- and plot-level compiled mensurational attributes for each ground plot across a series of repeated measurements. Both the PSP and non-PSP compilation outputs include a Data Dictionary that describes all the tables and attributes found in the downloadable files. The 'psp' dataset includes both inactive and active Permanent Sample Plot (PSP) data. The 'non-psp' dataset includes CMI, YSM, NFI, and VRI plots. The CMI, YSM and NFI plots are all located on a grid and only GENERALIZED COORDINATES are provided for …
forest-inventory-ground-plot-data-and-in.m:
Source ground plot data are stored in FAIB's Inventory Sample Management Consolidation (ISMC) data management system. Ground plot data in ISMC are continuously being added as hundreds of plots are being measured annually. These compilation outputs are updated periodically as milestones are reached in sampling (data entry completed, lab counted ages added) or where updates are made to the compiler or where key DataBC GIS layers used in the compiler are updated. Several GIS overlays are completed in the compilation process (BEC, Ownership, TSA, FIZ). The version of each of the layers used in these GIS overlays are outlined in the readme.txt file posted on the Compiled Ground Plot FTP site.

forest-inventory-ground-plots-public-acc.d:
The Forest Analysis and Inventory Branch (FAIB) is responsible for coordinating and managing data collection and analyses from a range of different ground sampling programs that collect data on ground plots. This layer shows ground plots from the PSP and VRI programs.

Vegetation Resource Inventory (VRI): ground samples primarily used to audit and verify key inventory attributes estimated during photo interpretation. These samples are not protected because they will not be revisited.

Permanent Sample Plots (PSP): subjectively located fixed-area permanent plots, valued for their long-term re-measurement data to support development of growth-and-yield models in unmanaged stands across a range of stand and ecosystem types. Actual GPS coordinates are provided as protection is necessary.
- Active PSPs = plot and buffer are protected from harvesting
- Inactive PSPs = not protected from harvesting
forest-inventory-ground-plots-public-acc.m: Data is collected using handheld electronic field recorders, validation is run real time so corrections can be made in the field and then data is loaded into the Inventory Sample Management Consolidation (ISMC) database.

forest-tenure-cutblock-polygons-fta-4-0.d: This is a spatial layer that reflects operational activities for cutblocks contained within harvesting authorities. The Forest Tenures Section (FTS) is responsible for the creation and maintenance of digital Forest Atlas files for the province of British Columbia encompassing Forest and Range Act Tenures. It also supports the forest resources programs delivered by MoFR. Each feature contains a Ministry of Forests and Range (MoFR) FEATURE_CLASS_SKEY (number) column that further defines the type of that feature. The layer contains cutblock boundaries for the following feature classes: Forest Licence Cut Block (555), Licence to Cut Cut Block (616), Timber Licence Cut Block (810), Timber Sale Licence Major Cut Block (817), Timber Sale Licence Minor CB Non Replaceable (820), Tree Farm Licence Cut Block (833), Wood Lot Licence Cut Block (863), Community Forest Cut Block (2402), and Timber Sale Licence Minor CB Replaceable (2417). Each cut block has a life cycle status that is either PENDING - the cut block has been submitted as a new cut block or an amendment, but is not yet approved or rejected, ACTIVE - the cut block is approved and activities may be taking place on the cut block, or RETIRED - all activities, with respect to the harvesting authority, have been completed for the cut block

freshwater-atlas-islands.d:
All island polygons. Islands may overlap as there are islands within islands (e.g., a lake on an island contains an island).

GNIS_NAME_1 contains the most atomic name for the island. For example, there are 3797 "Haida Gwaii" islands. If the island has not been named as part of a more specific group or with an individual name, "Haida Gwaii" is the GNIS_NAME_1 value. GNIS_NAME_2 and GNIS_NAME_3 values are null. If the island has a more specific name, "Haida Gwaii" moves to GNIS_NAME_2, and the more atomic name, such as "Moresby Island" is the GNIS_NAME_1. If the island has an individual name, belongs to a group, and is part of Haida Gwaii, the same logic of naming from most to least specific applies. For example, GNIS_NAME_1 = "George Island", GNIS_NAME_2 = "Copper Islands", GNIS_NAME_3 = "Haida Gwaii".

freshwater-fish-habitat-accessibility-mo.d:
The Freshwater Fish Habitat Accessibility MODEL- Pacific Salmon and Steelhead predicts the potential extent of accessible freshwater habitat for Pacific Salmon species and Steelhead in BC. Using the BC Freshwater Atlas as the mapping base, the model presumes that in watershed groups where a given species is known to occur, the species can potentially access any stream that is either:
- downstream of a known, validated fish observations for the given species
OR
- has no known barrier to fish passage downstream AND
- has no segment steeper (for at least 100m) than the known swimming ability of the given species anywhere downstream

This product is an ACCESSIBILITY MODEL only – it represents only the streams that Pacific Salmon and Steelhead could potentially use for migration, based on known/modelled barriers and the given species swimming ability. The model accounts only for natural barriers and connectivity – other essential characteristics for defining fish habitat are not included. For example, streams modelled as accessible may not have flow sufficient for supporting fish. As such, this model is not appropriate for use in operational applications. It is more appropriate for landscape level assessments and planning exercises. Site specific projects such as riparian buffer delineation require field assessment, stream measurements and fish sampling.
freshwater-fish-habitat-accessibility-mo.m:
The Freshwater Fish Habitat Accessibility MODEL has been under development for several years as part of the culvert fish passage project. The genesis of the project was the need to prioritize culvert assessment and remediation efforts in order to find the crossings that were likely to have the most habitat to be gained upstream of them.

The model has undergone a number of changes in both the approach and the input data over the years. A few examples include:

• Refined and improved the approaches to gradient calculation and gradient threshold definition

• Refined the use of Intermittent vs perennial flow

• Recognition of differences in modelling anadromous vs resident species

• Creation of this salmon species version – based on those specific species OBS and swimming ability

• Ongoing work to clean up fish OBS data to remove erroneous data points from the model

CRIMS is a legacy dataset of BC coastal resource data that was acquired in a systematic and synoptic manner from 1979 and was intermittently updated throughout the years. Glaciers is a multi-part polygon dataset representing the 2021 extent of glaciers in British Columbia.

This dataset may be used to represent the most current glacier extent for the province of British Columbia. It is anticipated that the dataset will be refreshed every few years based on more current imagery, and the previous version will be added to the Historical Glaciers (https://catalogue.data.gov.bc.ca/dataset/historical-glaciers) dataset.

For enquiries regarding this dataset, please refer to the Contacts section below.

For enquiries regarding the Open Licence - University of Northern British Columbia, contact research@unbc.ca.
glaciers.m: The Glaciers dataset has not been delineated based on flow lines, watersheds, or glacier name; rather, contiguous polygons have been merged (dissolved) into one mass. The dataset has been clipped to the political boundary of British Columbia (https://catalogue.data.gov.bc.ca/dataset/province-of-british-columbia-boundary-terrestrial/). The structure of the dataset facilitates comparisons of glacier extent, both of individual glaciers and at regional and provincial scales.

great-bear-rainforest-landscape-reserve-.d:
This layer contains current Landscape Reserve Design (LRD) polygons associated the Great Bear Rainforest. The spatial data layer excludes sensitive information and is publicly viewable and downloadable.
This data represents legally established and spatially defined LRD areas and are designed to meet Great Bear Rainforest requirements for Old Forest representation, Indigenous features and resources, wildlife values, and rare and endangered ecosystems that are identified during landscape unit planning or operational planning processes. Forest licensees are required to implement Ecosystem Based Management during operational planning processes to concurrently maintain ecosystem integrity and improve human well-being. This spatial view displays the current legal polygons, with more to be added as LRDs are established. This data is viewable in iMapBC by adding this layer name: *Landscape Reserve Design – GBRO - legal*.
great-bear-rainforest-landscape-reserve-.m: The LRDs begun establishment in 2021 and continue to be established. Amendment packages will be submitted by Licensees and reviewed by the Government-to-Government forum on an annual basis. This dataset will then be updated to reflect the approved amendments.

great-blue-herons-coastal-resource-infor.d: Distribution of Great Blue Heron habitat in coastal British Columbia showing relative abundance (RA) by season and overall relative importance (RI). RI is based on project region and not on the province as a whole. CRIMS is a legacy dataset of BC coastal resource data that was acquired in a systematic and synoptic manner from 1979 and was intermittently updated throughout the years. Resource information was collected in nine study areas using a peer-reviewed provincial Resource Information Standards Committee consisting of DFO Fishery Officers, First Nations, and other subject matter experts. There are currently no plans to update this legacy data.

NOTE: This dataset is the result of an analysis of many input layers and as such the accuracy, currency, and completeness of the dataset cannot be relied upon for operational use.

Please refer to the BC Cumulative Effects Northeast Region website for all cumulative effects related project information, as well as documents related to this dataset, such as protocols, reports and online tools: https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/environment/natural-resource-stewardship/cumulative-effects-framework/regional-assessments/northeast

The British Columbia Cumulative Effects Framework (BC CEF) Grizzly Bear 2015 Condition Assessment is a strategic, broad scale (provincial) assessment of the status of Grizzly Bear population and habitat indicators in 2015. The conceptual model used for this assessment is derived from the Interim Assessment Protocol for Grizzly Bear in British Columbia (Tier 1 Provincial Scale Grizzly Bear Assessment Protocol) prepared for British Columbia’s Cumulative Effects Framework Values Foundation Steering Committee, 2017 (https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/environment/natural-resource-stewardship/cumulative-effects-framework/value-assessments-protocols).

This dataset was generated from existing summaries of grizzly bear status, mortality data, Geographic Information System (GIS) data, and results from spatial modelling. The assessment units are the BC Landscape Units (see link below in Lineage Statement) to assess the mortality and habitat at the landscape …

For some CEF values, it may be the same as the ASSESSMENT_UNIT_SOURCE_ID. For example, for the Grizzly Bear value, this corresponds to the provincial Landscape …

For example, the ASSESSMENT_UNIT_GROUP For Grizzly Bear is the Grizzly Bear Population Unit (GBPU) with the maximum …

ASSESSMENT_TARGET_YEAR is the base year the assessment represents. This is typically the year, or vintage, of when the input data was collected, snapshot, or derived. An assessment processed in 2016 may be based on 2015 source data, therefore the target year would be 2015.

ASSESSED_AREA_STATUS is the status of whether the assessment was conducted in the Assessment Unit polygon or not, i.e., Assessed, Not Applicable (not applicable or required for that area, for example, the value does not exist there, or there is no target/policy for that area), Insufficient Data …
ASSESSMENT_UNIT_PROCESSED_DATE is the date when the GIS assessment analysis was run for the assessment unit. This may vary for assessment units throughout the province.

ASSESSMENT_VERSION_NUMBER is the alpha numeric version number assigned to the assessment, e.g. “01.00.01” where the numbers from left to right indicate decreasing amount of change from the previous version. See CEF Data Management Plan for more information.
BUSINESS_CONTACTS is the primary business area contact for this dataset.
GIS_CONTACTS is the primary GIS analyst contact for this dataset.
CEF_ONLINE_RESOURCES is a hyperlink to a webpage with additional information about the Cumulative Effects Framework.

PROTOCOL_DOCUMENT_LINK is a hyperlink to the CEF value protocol document associated with this dataset.
REPORTING UNIT MAX is the BC Cumulative Effects Sub-Regional Reporting Unit (RU) which has the maximum overlap with the assessment unit (AU), e.g., Merritt, Cariboo West.
NET AREA KM2 NO WATER ICE is the net assessment unit area, in square kilometres (km2), excluding major ice and water features from Baseline Thematic Mapping (BTM).

NET AREA KM2 NO WATER ICE ROCK is the net assessment unit area (km2), excluding major ice and water features from Baseline Thematic Mapping (BTM) and excluding upland rock from the Vegetation Resource Inventory (VRI).

COASTAL DISCONNECTED IND is an indicator for coastally disconnected (remote)areas which may have roads but are accessible only by ferry or water routes, i.e., Yes (coastally disconnected), No (not coastally disconnected).

GBPU MAX OVRLP PCNT is the percent overlap of the Grizzly Bear Population Unit (GBPU) that has the maximum (max) overlap with the AU.

GBPU OVRLP COUNT is the count of Girzzly Bear Population Units (GBPUs) which overlap the AU by more than 10%.

GBPU CRI OVRLP STATUS THREATND is the status of the Grizzly Bear Population Unit (GBPU) that overlaps with the AU (if >10% overlap) and that may be Threatened. Even if there is minor/minimum overlap with a Threatened GBPU, the AU will be considered Threatened (as opposed to Viable) for this field, …

WMU OVRLP COUNT is the count of WMUs which overlap the AU by more than 10%. It is the count of WMUs in the WMU_OVRLP_LIST.
GB EST POP is the estimated Grizzly Bear population (number of bears) for the AU.
GB EST POP DENS is the estimated Grizzly Bear population density (number of bears / 1000 km2) for the AU.
GB EST POP DENS CLS is the classification of estimated bear population density, i.e., 1 ( 0-<10 bears/1000 km2), 2 (10-<20), 3 (20-<30), 4 (30-<40), 5 (40-<50), 6 (50+).
GB EST POP DENS FLAG is a flag for whether or not the bear density is less than 10 bears per 1000 km2, i.e., Pass (Bear Density >=10 per 1000km2), Fail (Bear Density <10 per 1000km2).

The maximum count is 6. Allocation periods cover 2004-2006, 2007-2011, and 2012-2014. If the AU overlaps …

HUNTER DAYS ANNL AVG is the average annual hunter days between 2003 and 2012 for the AU. Based on Wildlife Management Unit (WMU) data, but extrapolated to AU based on the number of days per square km for the WMU.
HUNTER DAYS ANNL AVG DENS is the derived average annual hunter day density for the AU (HUNTER_DAYS_ANNL_AVG/NET_AREA_KM2_NO_WATER_ICE).

HUNTER DAYS ANNL AVG DENS CLS is the classification of average annual hunter day density, based on division of values into quartiles (Q), i.e., Low (Q1 and Q2: 0-0.601977), Mod (Q3: 0.601978 - 1.508812), High (Q4: >1.508812).

From 2018 on, NatureServe conservation concern ranking categories (e.g., Very Low, Low, Moderate, High, Extreme Concern) supersede the pre-2018 population status categories (e.g., Viable, Threatened, Extirpated) contained in the field STATUS. The Grizzly Bear Population Units (GBPU) polygon boundaries in this datasets go back to the year 2003. The previous GBPU boundary versions are from 2003a, 2003b, 2005 and 2012.

The 2015 boundary adjustments were directed by Tony Hamilton (Wildlife Biologist) and prepared by Sasha Lees (GIS).

The 2018 version has no boundary changes, but uses the Conservation Ranking attributes. The 2018 boundaries and population estimates were used in the 2018 provincial Cumulative Effects Assessment.

The 2020 version includes a boundary update for the Kitlope-Fiordland GBPU, directed by Garth Mowat (Wildlife & Habitat Branch) and prepared by Rajiv Lalla (GIS).

ground-water-well-capture-zones.m: The capture zones have been delineated by different hydrogeologists using different methodologies such as arbitrary fixed radius, calculated fixed radius, analytical equations and numerical modelling. Time of travel (TOT) zones have been delineated by different hydrogeologists and are not all the same. Some of the capture zones delineated by arbitrary fixed radius or analytical equation may not have a time of travel associated with the boundary delineated. For others, TOT zones have been categorized in this coverage using different colours, e.g., red for </=1 year, yellow for >1 to </= 5 years, green for >5 to </= 10 years and blue for >10 years. Capture zones with no associated time of travel are purple. These coloured polygons represent the TOT zones delineated by the hydrogeologist that falls within the TOT category; the TOT zone may or may not correspond to the category boundaries. …

Main entry for water into the well, i.e., open bottom, uncased hole, and screen.
Owner of the water supply system using the well, e.g., Township of Langley, Cedar Lake Water System, Copperside Estates.
Well name or identifier used by the water supply system, e.g., Well#5, north well, pine street well.

The date that the well construction was completed.

The date that alteration works, such as increasing the well depth or diameter, were completed.

growth-and-yield-plots-active-status.d:
This layer is the authoritative source for locating Active Status Growth and Yield plots also known as Permanent Sample Plots (PSPs). These plots are protected and require an additional minimum windfirm buffer of 50m radius in the interior and 100m radius on the coast. These plots are generally 16m radius fixed area plots. Therefore, protected areas need to be a minimum of 66m radius around the plot centre in the interior and 116m radius on the coast. Best practices are to locate the plot centre on the ground as coordinate accuracy varies.

The program now maintains partially damaged plots in order to provide critical data on how partially damaged plots grow over time. Therefore, salvage logging is NOT permitted within protected plots.

Please contact Anya Reid (Anya.Reid@gov.bc.ca) with questions or updated coordinates for plots.

NOTE: Accuracy of the coordinates are variable. Coordinates for plots with a more recent (since 2000) last measurement are generally quite accurate (3m). However, plots measured in the 1990's have a wide range of coordinate accuracy. In all cases, it is necessary to ground truth plot location before block layout. In this spatial layer, low accuracy coordinates are buffered 300m to ensure they do not get missed from development planning.

This layer replaces the Growth and Yield Samples – Active Status (https://catalogue.data.gov.bc.ca/dataset/0ca49478-5d0f-44e8-b6af-3fd6e387803c) layer with more accurate and current information from the Inventory …
growth-and-yield-plots-active-status.m: This dataset goes back 90 years. Data collection and storage has changed over time. Originally PSP data were collected by hand on field forms and then key punched into a computer in Standard Edit Format (ASCII flat file). This was replaced with data being collected using Handheld computer, validated using Sample Plot Tools and loaded to the GYS Oracle database. Currently, data is collected using updated handheld electronic field recorders, validation is run real time so corrections can be made in the field and then data is loaded into the ISMC database.

herring-spawn-coastal-resource-informati.d: Coastline segments indicating herring spawing sites along the coastline of British Columbia. Attribute information includes relative importance, spawing frequency and spawn index. CRIMS is a legacy dataset of BC coastal resource data that was acquired in a systematic and synoptic manner from 1979 and was intermittently updated throughout the years. Resource information was collected in nine study areas using a peer-reviewed provincial Resource Information Standards Committee consisting of DFO Fishery Officers, First Nations, and other subject matter experts. There are currently no plans to update this legacy data.

historic-environment-spatial-layer.d:
The Historic Environment Spatial Layer contains polygons and related attributes representing post-1846 historic places in British Columbia that are recorded on the provincial heritage register. It does not include any archaeological site information.

This dataset was replaced by the Historic Places Spatial Layer (Public View) (https://catalogue.data.gov.bc.ca/dataset/fc2b29ff-89a4-490b-bf7c-8d3e2f2af5d4) and Historic Places Spatial Layer (Internal View) (https://catalogue.data.gov.bc.ca/dataset/80fe81a8-05fa-4bcc-bbb5-b09ae4b8e65b) in March 2024.

c: HISTORIC ENVIRONMENT ID is a system generated unique identification number. This is a primary key of this dataset.
HISTORIC ENVIRONMENT SITE ID is a user maintained unique identification number.

BORDENNUMBER is the unique site number. In BC, all archaeological sites and historic places are coded using the Borden system in which each location is assigned a sequence of 4 letters (e.g., DcRu) relating to a fixed map grid, and a number (e.g., 631) based on the sequence of recording of the site …

HISTORIC SITE IND is an indicator of whether or not the site is a formally recognized historic place, i.e., Y or N where Y means the site has formal recognition from some level of government (local, provincial or federal) and N means the site is known to exist but has not been formally recognized.
REGISTRATION STATUS is an indicator of the site's registration status on the provincial heritage register, i.e., Registered, Federal Jurisdiction, or Legacy.
COMMON SITE NAME lists the name most commonly used for the site, e.g., Royal Roads University.

OTHER SITE NAMES lists the other names of the site such as an aboriginal name, a historic name, an official name, a name assigned by an owner (e.g., Rose Cottage), or a street address (e.g., 107 King Street) if any. More than one site name can be listed in this field separated by ';', e.g., Former …
PARCEL DESCRIPTION contains one or more parcel identifiers (PID) or a description of the parcel, e.g., 024874132; 024874124 or 8 lots - see VanMap.
STREET NUMBER is the street number of the site, e.g., 2870.
STREET NAME is the street name of the site, e.g., West 47th Avenue.
LOCALITY is the city or town in which the site is located, e.g., Barkerville.
PROVINCE is the province in which the site is located, i.e., BC for all records in this dataset.

JURISDICTION NAMES lists the names of the jurisdictions in which the site is located. More than one jurisdiction name can be listed in this field separated by ';', e.g., GIS Municipalities: Victoria; GIS RegionalDistrict: Capital.
RECOGNITION GOVERNMENT is the name of the government entity that formally recognized the site, e.g., Province of British Columbia, City of Vancouver, Cariboo Regional District.
RECOGNITION GOVERNMENT LEVEL is the level of government that formally recognized the site, i.e., Municipal, Provincial, Federal or World.
RECOGNITION TYPE is the type of protection or recognition used to protect or formally recognize the site, e.g., Heritage Designation.
RECOGNITION START DATE is the date on which the formal recognition was approved or took effect.
CONSTRUCTION YEAR is the year of construction of the historic place, if known. If the exact year is not known, an approximate date is displayed, e.g., 1958.
CONSTRUCTION YEAR QUALIFIER is the qualifier for the date displayed in the CONSTRUCTION YEAR column. There are five possible qualifiers: After, Before, Circa, Exact or .
CONSTRUCTION YEAR DATETTYPE is the date type listed in the CONSTRUCTION YEAR column. There are four options: Assessed Date, Construction, Construction (circa) or Significant.
STMT OF SIGNIFICANCE DESC is a brief description of the historic place as it exists today. It also identifies the boundaries of the formally-recognized area.
CRHP IND is an indicator of whether or not this site is listed on the Canadian Register of Historic Places (CRHP), i.e., Y or N.

ARCHITECT NAMES lists the names of the architects or designers of the site, if known. More than one architect or designer name can be listed in this field separated by ';', e.g., Public Works Department; RCMP.
BUILDER NAMES lists the name of the builder of the site, if known. More than one builder name can be listed in this field separated by ';', e.g., Galbraith; Smith, Roland.
CURRENT FUNCTIONAL CATEGORIES lists the current functional categories of the site, if known. More than one functional category can be listed in this field separated by ';', e.g., Community; Leisure.

HISTORIC FUNCTIONAL CATEGORIES lists the historic functional categories of the site, if known. More than one functional category can be listed in this field separated by ';', e.g., Community; Industry.
AREA HECTARES is the total area of the historic place as recorded on provincial GIS, measured in hectares, e.g., 578.81293.
FEATURE AREA SQM is the system calculated area of a two-dimensional polygon in square meters.
FEATURE LENGTH M is the system calculated length or perimeter of a geometry in meters.
SHAPE is the column used to reference the spatial coordinates defining the feature.
OBJECTID is a column required by spatial layers that interact with ESRI ArcSDE. It is populated with unique values automatically by SDE.
SE ANNO CAD DATA is a binary column used by spatial tools to store annotation, curve features and CAD data when using the SDO GEOMETRY storage data type.

historic_places_public_view.d:
The dataset includes polygons and attributes of all officially recognized historic sites in British Columbia that are post-1846 heritage sites registered on the BC Register of Historic Places as a statutory requirement of the Heritage Conservation Act. Historic places include buildings, neighbourhoods, trails, and cultural landscapes that contribute to BC’s unique identity and history.

This dataset includes historic places in British Columbia that have been officially recognized for their heritage values at the local government, provincial, and/or federal level through heritage conservation legislation under the Heritage Conservation Act, the Local Government Act, Vancouver Charter, Historic Sites and Monuments Act, etc.

This dataset does not include any archaeological site information. Please contact the Archaeology Branch for information on archaeological sites in British Columbia.

Note: This dataset replaces the Historic Environment Spatial Layer

historical-glaciers.d:
Historical Glaciers is a multi-part polygon dataset representing the circa 1985 extent of glaciers in British Columbia.

Please refer to the Glaciers (https://catalogue.data.gov.bc.ca/dataset/glaciers) dataset to represent recent glacier extent for the province of British Columbia. It is anticipated that the Glaciers (https://catalogue.data.gov.bc.ca/dataset/glaciers) dataset will be refreshed every few years based on more current imagery, and the previous version will be added to the Historical Glaciers dataset.

For enquiries regarding this dataset, please refer to the Contacts section below.

For enquiries regarding the Open Licence - University of Northern British Columbia, contact research@unbc.ca.
historical-glaciers.m: The Historical Glaciers dataset has not been delineated based on flow lines, watersheds, or name; rather, contiguous polygons have been merged (dissolved) into one mass. The dataset has been clipped to the political boundary of British Columbia (https://catalogue.data.gov.bc.ca/dataset/province-of-british-columbia-boundary-terrestrial/). The structure of the dataset facilitates comparisons of glacier extent, both of individual glaciers and at regional and provincial scales.

historical-open-range-1963-1994.d: Historical Open Range - 1963-1994 is a polygon layer that depicts grasslands and shrublands (originally designated as 'on land deemed with no potential for growing trees'). Data were derived from a (retired) Provincial Forest Cover Polygon dataset which was interpreted from air photos. Photograph and interpretation dates range from 1963 to 1994. This dataset has value as temporal snapshots of ecosystems under siege from human and natural processes. Data is useful for identification and analysis of forest ingrowth into grasslands from fire suppression. Encroachment can shift over time, for example from changing climate and disturbance events, and this data provides one measure of that shift. Data may also inform location of wildfire safety buffers around communities.

hpai-detections-in-bc-wildlife.d:
This dataset contains surveillance information for wildlife in British Columbia that have been tested and confirmed to carry the highly pathogenic avian influenza virus of the H5 subtype.

Fields include:
Species_Group - Bird or Mammal
Species - Animal species
Y_Latitude - Latitude
X_Longitude - Longitude
Sample_Type - Indicates the source of the sample. Categories are as follows: "WBS" for passive wild bird surveillance on wildlife found dead, "Feces" for swabs taken directly from wild bird feces, "Live" for swabs collected directly from live captured and released wildlife, "Hunted" for swabs collected from hunter-harvested carcasses, "Captive" for swabs collected from captive or privately-owned wild bird species such as breeding colonies of spotted owls
Date_Found - Date the animal was found
Date_Swabbed - Date the sample was swabbed for testing
HPAI - Yes/No. Whether the sample is considered to have highly pathogenic AIV or not.
HA_subtype - Subtype results for hemagglutinin gene (HA) by way of sequencing
genomic_cluster - Genomic clustering by way of sequencing
YQ - Year and Quarter

AIV monitoring in wildlife is conducted by BC WASP (the BC Wildlife Avian Influenza Surveillance Program), which is a collaboration among the BC Ministry of Agriculture and Food, the BC Ministry of Forests, the BC Centre for Disease Control, and the Canadian Wildlife Service.

human-disturbance-2025.d:
The human disturbance dataset (previously known as the Cumulative Effects Framework Human Disturbance) aims to create a consolidated footprint of human activity on the landscape of British Columbia. It is intended to support landscape-level (coarse) analysis.

The dataset captures disturbances from the resource industries (mining, oil and gas, forestry), infrastructure (power and railways), urban development, recreation and agriculture. It does not capture road or natural (wildfire or pests) disturbances. Road disturbance is captured in the complementary dataset (integrated roads), which is available through the DataBC Catalogue (https://catalogue.data.gov.bc.ca/dataset/a489bc6a-f676-4503-8cd7-dcf0bdf2ae99).

The human disturbance analysis is a flattened representation in which disturbance is reported hierarchically by permanence. More permanent or current disturbances (forestry only) are given higher ranks than less permanent or older disturbances. When two disturbance types overlap, the more permanent takes priority. *Due to this approach, it is not possible to determine the total hectares of a single disturbance.*

All methodologies are reproducible and are from publicly accessible data with varying levels of quality, accuracy and completeness. Please refer to the attached methodology and accompanying spreadsheet listing the input data sources under "Data and Resources".

hydrology-hydrometric-watershed-boundari.d:
Watershed boundary delineated for Canada-BC hydrometric stations.
Currently, watersheds were delineated using 1:50,000 scale boundaries in 1996, and many watersheds encompass entire drainages, instead of just the upstream watersheds.
Note - Not yet available, but we are in the process of generating BC hydrometric station upstream watersheds using updated base data, using the following method:
Within BC, watershed boundaries are based on the 1:20,000-scale Freshwater Atlas fundamental watersheds, and trimmed using the BC TRIM DEM used to approximate the height-of-land at the station locations. Outside of BC, but within Canada, watershed boundaries were approximated using Canada CDED DEM data for delineation (no "stream burning" was used) and some manual editing of boundaries was done to approximately match hydrology data after the fact. Within U.S.A., the USGS Watershed Boundary Dataset was used (at the best scale available for each drainage) to delineate the watershed boundary, with the watershed trimmed using the USGS National Elevation Dataset to approximate the height-of-land when necessary.

ice-flow-indicator-compilation.d: Building on previous ice-flow indicator compilations for British Columbia, this map and database illustrate major ice-flow directions for the Canadian sector of the Cordilleran ice sheet during the Late Pleistocene. The data were derived from published and unpublished surficial geology, terrain, and glacial feature maps. Because field data are sparse in the area ~ 300 km south of the British Columbia -Yukon border, new data were generated using digital stereo airphotos, digital derived-stereo orthophoto mosaics, and digital derived-stereo Satellite Pour l'Observation de la Terre (SPOT) imagery. The raw data are integrated into a single database; no attempt was made to reconcile cases where data from different sources conflict. The integrated database is published as BCGS Open File 2016-04 and the 152,000 ice-flow directional features are displayed on MapPlace.

This tabular dataset is the result of an analysis completed for the Roads & Roadless Areas in B.C. indicator published on Environmental Reporting BC (http://www.env.gov.bc.ca/soe/indicators/land/roads.html).

Roaded and roadless areas were determined using the B.C. Digital Road Atlas (https://catalogue.data.gov.bc.ca/dataset/bb060417-b6e6-4548-b837-f9060d94743e), the best available single source of road data for British Columbia. The analysis was done on Digital Road Atlas data available as of May 1st, 2018. All paved roads and unpaved roads and trails that *allow* motorized vehicle use—as detailed in the Digital Road Atlas Data Dictionary (https://catalogue.data.gov.bc.ca/dataset/bb060417-b6e6-4548-b837-f9060d94743e)—were included in the analysis. Some road features available in the Digital Road Atlas (https://catalogue.data.gov.bc.ca/dataset/bb060417-b6e6-4548-b837-f9060d94743e) were excluded, including non-roads (ferry routes, proposed roads, pedestrian only roads, non-motorized trails and water access routes) and non-active roads (decommissioned and overgrown roads). Roaded areas were defined as areas within 500 metres of a road. Roadless areas were defined as areas greater than 500 metres from a road.

Areas are reported in hectares to three significant figures for two distance classes: 0 to 500m from a road (roaded) and greater than 500m from a road (not roaded) for British Columbia and for each ecoregion …

These tabular datasets are the result of an analysis completed for the 'Land Designations that Contribute to Conservation in B.C.' indicator (http://www.env.gov.bc.ca/soe/indicators/land/land-designations.html) published on Environmental Reporting BC.

Land designations that contribute to conservation are spatially-defined areas established through legislation or purchased for the protection of nature and cultural values, the conservation of biological diversity and ecosystem services and the management of natural resources. Over 40 land designations were divided into three broad categories:

- Protected Lands includes all _Parks & Protected Areas_ with the primary purpose of the long-term conservation of nature and cultural values. This category includes a subcategory called _Other Protected Lands_ which are those Protected Lands not managed by a Parks agency (For example, lands held Non-Governmental Organizations).

- Resource Exclusion Areas includes all designations that fully exclude one or two resource activities for the purpose of conservation.

- Spatially Managed Areas includes all spatial designations managing or limiting development or a resource activity for the purpose of conservation, or a spatial management regime in place to preserve specified elements of biodiversity but where activity is still allowed to occur.

This record contains tabular summaries of the area and percentage of land in each of the categories, at a provincial scale as well as by …

indicator-summary-data-trends-in-timber-.d:
This dataset contains the results reported for the Trends in Timber Harvesting indicator (http://www.env.gov.bc.ca/soe/indicators/land/timber-harvest.html) published on Environmental Reporting BC.

The Timber Harvesting Indicator illustrates how much timber is harvested annually and how the actual timber harvest compares with the Allowable Annual Cut (AAC). The AAC information is derived from the Timber Supply Review (TSR) determination process for each Timber Supply Area. Timber harvest is derived from Harvest Billing System. All data used are summarized and rolled up at a high level. This indicator is a composite from the Timber Supply Review process and the Harvest Billing System. The provincial Timber Supply Forecast is a summary of the management unit harvest forecast data. None of the data used to create timber harvest indicator can be traced back to sole harvest areas or designated tenures. These datasets are derived from the ministry’s own data source and have been created by government employees.

inter-provincial-and-international-migra.d:
Estimated inter-provincial and international migration flows for B.C. updated quarterly. Customizable data tables and data visualizations are provided via BC Stats' Migration App (https://bcstats.shinyapps.io/interprovincial_migration_bc/).

Last quarter update: 2026 Q1 (January - March)

For international migration:

Total number of individuals leaving BC = Emigrants + Net Temporary Emigrants – Returning Emigrants

Total number moving to BC = International Immigrants + Net Non Permanent Residents.

Note: As part of the 2023 Q2 update, Statistics Canada revised its calculation methods for estimating the numbers of emigrants and returning emigrants going back to 2016 Q2. Before this date, short-term emigrants and short-term returning emigrants are included in the “Net Temporary Emigrants” component. After this date, they are included in the "Emigrants" and "Returning Emigrants" components using a different estimation methodology than previously. Due to this change, the "Net Temporary Emigrants" component is calculated as zero from 2016 Q3 onwards. Emigrant and returning emigrant estimates for periods before 2016 Q3 are not entirely comparable to subsequent estimates.

isotopic-age-determinations-for-rock-uni.d:
BCAge database contains all reported non-proprietary isotopic age determinations for bedrock units from British Columbia, Alberta, Washington and Alaska. The database contains 7759 age determinations from 4828 rock samples, summarizing 622 published articles, theses or unpublished reports. The data is fully relational, and may be queried by the user on the basis absolute age (in Ma), location (NTS mapsheet, terrane polygon, or decimal lat-long, as specified by the user) or source (e.g. author, journal title, etc.). This data has also been integrated into MapPlace and is available as an MS Access database in BCGS Open File 2004-03. This 2004 compilation is also available in a flat tabular format for ease of use.

A 2020 publication (BCGS GeoFile 2020-10) add 532 ages from 66 papers and reports from the BC Geological Survey, Geoscience BC, and external publications. The ages were determined using ten mineral-isotopic systems and six dating methods, predominantly U-Pb zircon. This release contains two CSV files and one Microsoft Access file. The CSV files, one for new data (new_age_2020.csv) the other for BCAge data (bc_age_2020.csv), were generated with simplicity, exchangeability, and GIS-readiness in mind. They contain sample location coordinates, age, and numerous other primary attributes. The Microsoft Access database file, which is available through the GF2020-10 publication link, includes entities, and relationships, and metadata.

The 2020 compilation is: Han, T., Ootes, L., and Yun, K. 2020. The new British Columbia Geological Survey geochronologic database: Preliminary release of ages. British Columbia Ministry of Energy, Mines and Petroleum Resources, British Columbia Geological Survey GeoFile 2020-10.

The historical data sets for the years 1974, 77, 78, 79 and 80 and more recent data sets collected from 2001 to 2016, and 2018. The historical data was derived from information collected in the field and hand drawn onto air photographs. Ministry staff circled Okanagan Lake in a boat one time each year and recorded fish numbers and spawner locations onto air photographs that were digitized in 2006 to make up the historical data set. This data set may not capture the peak reach count for these years. The data collected from 2001 to 2018 was derived from boat counts undertaken along the shoreline of Okanagan, Wood and Kalamalka Lakes. A GPS was used to record shore spawner locations and numbers. Multiple counts were undertaken over the entire spawning cycle and covered the peak spawning period for each year of data provided. The data collected for Christina Lake began in 2003 and ended in 2006. Christina Lake kokanee spawn at night in late December and early January. Kokanee spawning redd locations are available for the 2003/2004 count. Kokanee enumerations were undertaken at night for the 2004/2005 and 2005/2006 seasons and spawning redds were counted at the end of spawning cycle. For these two years there is both spawning and redd count data available.

land-designations-that-contribute-to-con.d:
NOTE: Not for operational use. This dataset is the result of an analysis (Aug 2018) of many input layers and as such the accuracy, currency, and completeness of the dataset cannot be relied upon for operational or management decision making.

Land designations that contribute to conservation are spatially-defined areas established through legislation or purchased for the protection of nature and cultural values, the conservation of biological diversity and ecosystem services and the management of natural resources.

Over 40 land designations were divided into three broad categories:

- Protected Lands includes all Parks & Protected Areas and Other Protected Lands with the primary purpose of the long-term conservation of nature and cultural values.

- Resource Exclusion Areas includes all designations that fully exclude one or two resource activities for the purpose of conservation.

- Spatially Managed Areas includes all spatial designations managing or limiting development or a resource activity for the purpose of conservation, or a spatial management regime in place to preserve specified elements of biodiversity but where activity is still allowed to occur.

Land designations layers were combined into a single layer, with overlaps removed such that areas with overlapping designations were assigned to the highest conservation contribution category.

landscape-units-of-british-columbia-curr.d: Landscape Units are spatially identified areas of land and/or water used for long-term planning of resource management activities. Landscape units are important for designing strategies and objectives to maintain landscape level biodiversity and for managing other forest resources. Landscape units are also used to initiate landscape unit plans, which provide direction on biodiversity, old growth forest retention, wildlife habitat maintenance and timber harvesting. LUs may also be used as planning zones for other stakeholders in addition to forest licensees and MOFR. This spatial view was created based on the selection from the layer LANDSCAPE UNIT SP, where the DATE OF RETIREMENT is null. Therefore, only current LU shapes are included in this layer

licensed-gaming-revenues-earned-by-class.d: Eligible community organizations may hold licensed gaming events to generate revenue that benefits programs and services they deliver. Class A licensed ticket raffles are those that are expected to generate gross revenue of more than $20,000. Net revenue is determined from revenue reports submitted after the gaming event has finished. Revenue information submitted after the cutoff date for a given fiscal year is not included in this report. Registered raffles: anticipated gross revenue is $250,000 or more. Major raffles: anticipated gross revenue is $100,000 or more, but less than $250,000. Minor raffles: anticipated gross revenue is more than $20,000 and less than $100,000. Gaming event licences are associated with government fiscal years based on their 'end date'.

limited-entry-hunting-leh-zones-current-.d: Current Limited Entry Hunting (LEH) Zones polygons are hunting opportunities created via a lottery, and the details are found in the LEH Synopsis. Participation in the LEH draw is available to any resident of BC who legally possesses a BC Resident Hunter Number. The purpose of Limited Entry Hunting is to achieve wildlife management objectives without resorting to such measures as shortening seasons or completely closing areas. It is only introduced where it has become necessary to limit the number of hunters, limit the number of animals that may be taken, or limit the harvest to a certain class of animal. The Zones are valid during the LEH hunting season, and changes are made effective July 1st of each yearly. Some zones change frequently, some change rarely.

lithogeochemical-database.d: A new database system was developed to maintain, update, and manage province-wide lithogeochemical data collected by British Columbia Geological Survey (BCGS) geoscientists and their research partners. The database, released as BCGS GeoFile 2016-04, is populated with data compiled from 214 BCGS publications released between 1986 and 2015. It includes 10,914 samples with about 250,000 determinations analyzed by 26 analytical methods in 21 laboratories. The database operates through a semi-automated process for data compilation, quality control, upload, and product generation, which helps provide consistent, standardized, and long-term data storage and update, and regular release. The data product derived from the database provided in this release is in a user-friendly format (CVS), which can be easily brought into GIS and geochemical data evaluation software for visualization and analysis.

An approximate estimate of the capacity of the well to produce groundwater. Estimated by the well driller during construction by conducting a well yield test.

The unit of measure used for the well yield. As of April 2019 well yields are reported in U.S. Gallons per Minute. Prior to April 2019, well yield units vary or are unknown, e.g., U.S. Gallons per Minute, Gallons per Hour (U.S./Imperial), Dry Hole, Unknown Yield.
The level (depth below top of casing) to which water will naturally rise in a well without pumping, measured in feet, e.g. 280.0

The diameter of the casing of the well, measured in inches, e.g. 6.62. There can be multiple casings in a well, e.g. surface casing, and production casing. Diameter of casing made available to the public is generally the production casing.

System generated unique sequential number assigned to each mapped aquifer. The aquifer ID identifies which aquifer a well is in. An aquifer can have multiple wells, while a single well can only be in one aquifer.
GEOMETRY is the column used to reference the spatial coordinates defining the feature.
OBJECTID is a column required by spatial layers that interact with ESRI ArcSDE. It is populated with unique values automatically by SDE.

livestock-at-large-regulations-in-britis.d:
In British Columbia, there are over 100 Livestock Districts, Bull Control Areas and Pound Districts established by regulation under the Livestock Act. Livestock Districts, with minor exceptions, are areas where livestock may run at large within the district boundaries. Bull Control Areas are areas within Livestock District, in which Bull Control Committees may make rules respecting the number, breed, breeding, quality and age of bulls allowed to run at large. Pound Districts are areas where keepers, peace officers and others may impound animals at large, and allow for the sale of unclaimed impounded animals and the reimbursement of the keeper.

The regulations are published in the British Columbia Gazette Part II. The current Index of Current B.C. Regulations provides a complete list. Search Orders in Council from http://BCLaws.ca to view related Orders in Council including metes and bounds descriptions.

files.n: Livestock at Large in BC, web map application

c: LIVESTOCK ACT DIST ID is an operationally generated unique identification number.
ADMIN AREA NAME is the authoritative, officially approved name given to an administrative area, e.g., Okanagan-Keremeos.
ADMIN AREA TYPE is a low-level grouping of administrative areas used to categorise features by regulation type, e.g., Livestock District, Pound District, Bull Control Area.
ADMIN AREA STATUS is the status of the area in legislation, i.e., Active, Deleted, Retired, Under review, Pre Order in Council, Unknown.

ADMIN AREA GRP NAME is name given to the larger administrative area (if there is any) of which this feature is a member, e.g., Province of BC would be the ADMIN AREA GROUP NAME of most Livestock Districts.

BC REGULATION NUMBER is a chronologically ordered (ascending) semicolon-delimited list of B.C. regulations for an area. Starting in 2000, regulations numbers use the full four digit year. For those deposited or filed before 2000, the last two digits of the year are used, e.g. 516/59 denotes B.C. …

OIC NUMBER is a chronologically ordered (ascending) semicolon-delimited list of the Order-In-Council (OIC) identifiers for an area. The OIC NUMBER is in the form ####-YYYY where #### is a number that may contain leading zeros, then a dash '-' followed by a four-digit Year, e.g., 0730-1976

AMENDMENT NOTE is a chronologically ordered (ascending) semicolon-delimited list of notes on amendments for an area that do not have an Order-In-Council (OIC) number. Each amendment note should include the location of the amendment and the deposit date, e.g., paper file-deposited 1983.
AFFECTED ADMIN AREA ABRVN is a semicolon-delimited list of abbreviations of administrative areas boundaries that are affected by the OIC, e.g., SMLK PD; V PD (Similkameen and Vernon Pound Districts).
UPDATE TYPE is a short description of the latest alteration of the feature's geographic or attribute content, e.g., Inserted (new), Change in geometry.
UPDATE DATE is the date and time the digital record was last modified.
UPDATE COMMENTS is freehand technician comments on the alteration of the feature's geographic or attribute content.
FEATURE AREA SQM is the system calculated area of a two-dimensional polygon in square meters.
FEATURE LENGTH M is the system calculated length or perimeter of a geometry in meters.
SHAPE is the column used to reference the spatial coordinates defining the feature.

lobbyists-registry-open-datasets.d:
The Office of the Registrar of Lobbyists has oversight over the administration of the Lobbyists Transparency Act, which supports transparent, accountable lobbying in British Columbia. Here you will find open data sets on Lobbying Registration Returns and Lobbying Activity Reports in British Columbia as entered into the publicly searchable Lobbyists Registry. The use of the data sets on this website is subject to the Open Data Licence Agreement – Office of the Registrar of Lobbyists for British Columbia (ORL)

Both datasets provide primary compressed files containing secondary files in xlsx format. Also available for both are data dictionary files, which provide definitions for all data elements contained within the dataset.

Lobbying Registration Returns:
Consultant lobbyists and organizations that have in-house lobbyists are required to file a Registration Return within 10 days of beginning to lobby a public office holder. This dataset contains all lobbying Registration Returns filed with the ORL since 2010 and is updated monthly.

Lobbying Activity Reports:
Consultant lobbyists and organizations that have in-house lobbyists are required to disclose specific instances of lobbying communications with senior public office holders in British Columbia. These Lobbying Activity Reports must be filed no later than 15 days after the end of the month in which the lobbying activity occurred. The requirement to file Lobbying Activity Reports came into effect on May 4, 2020. This …

Archived lobbying information from 2002-2010 can be found on the Office of the Registrar of Lobbyists website: https://www.lobbyistsregistrar.bc.ca/the-registry/what-is-the-lobbyists-registrys-purpose/

local-and-regional-greenspaces.d: This dataset contains spatial and attribute information for local and regional greenspaces in British Columbia. Local and regional greenspaces are municipal or regional district lands designated by local government agencies and managed for public enjoyment, ecosystem or wildlife values. Spatial boundaries were sourced from municipal and regional district web sites, which in some cases provide datasets under Open Government Licence, and in other cases, publicize parks and greenspaces on web maps or pdf maps. Boundaries were edge-matched to the ParcelMap BC cadastre. This spatial layer contains multipart polygons.

c: LOCAL_REG_GREENSPACE_ID is a system-generated unique identification number.
PARK NAME is the name of the park, e.g., Allenby Park.
PARK_TYPE is the type of park, e.g., Local, Regional, Regional Reserve, Private.

PARK PRIMARY USE defines the primary use of a park, whether it is a general use park or there is a specific primary use, e.g., School, Pedestrian Walkway, Golf, Civic Plaza. The default value of Park is used for general use parks and where no specific primary use has been identified.
REGIONAL_DISTRICT is the name of the regional district in which the park resides, e.g., Capital Regional District.

MUNICIPALITY is the name of the municipality in which the park resides, or in which the majority of the park resides, e.g., Kamloops. If the value is null, the park is not within municipal boundaries.
CIVIC_NUMBER is the street number or nearest estimate of a street number for the park.
CIVIC_NUMBER_SUFFIX is the letter or fraction that may come after the CIVIC NUMBER, e.g., A, 1/2.
STREET_NAME is the name of the street or nearest street to the park, e.g., Burnside Rd W.
LATITUDE is the geographic coordinate, in decimal degrees (dd.dddddd), of the location of the feature as measured from the equator, e.g., 55.323653.
LONGITUDE is the geographic coordinate, in decimal degrees (dd.dddddd), of the location of the feature as measured from the prime meridian, e.g., -123.093544.
WHEN_UPDATED is the date and time the record was last modified.
WEBSITE_URL contains a link to the home page of the park or the parks department, where available.

LICENCE_COMMENTS describes the source of the data where open data restrictions specify that attribution statements must be used, e.g., Contains information licensed under the Open Government Licence - City of Surrey.
FEATURE_AREA_SQM is the system calculated area of a two-dimensional polygon in square meters.
FEATURE_LENGTH_M is the system calculated length or perimeter of a geometry in meters.
SHAPE is the column used to reference the spatial coordinates defining the feature.
OBJECTID is a column required by spatial layers that interact with ESRI ArcSDE. It is populated with unique values automatically by SDE.

local-area-economic-profiles-custom-cens.d:
These contain the source data for BC Stats' 2025 Local Area Economic Profiles (LAEP) project. It is the original, unmodified custom census data obtained from Statistics Canada.
It is employment, employment income, and average employment income data from the last three Canadian Census periods (2021, 2016 and 2011); arranged by industry at the 4-digit NAICS level; for British Columbia, 29 B.C. Census Divisions, and 103 custom local areas (a.k.a. Economic Dependency Areas, EDAs) used in the LAEP project.
The documents are in IVT format, which can be accessed with the Beyond 20/20 application (https://www.statcan.gc.ca/en/public/beyond20-20), available for download from Statistics Canada at the link below.

If you need help with this dataset, you can reach BC Stats at the email below; however, submitting a support request is recommended.

Source: Statistics Canada, Census 2021, accessed July 2024. Reproduced and distributed on an "as is" basis with the permission of Statistics Canada.
fl: Data only as PDF, web pages or images

local-area-economic-profiles-dataset.d:
This is the complete dataset of the 2025 Local Area Economic Profiles (LAEP) project by BC Stats, which provides detailed information on 103+ sub-provincial areas. For more information on data concepts and methodology, follow the link to BC Stats' website.
It is the data in CSV format that is also contained in the LAEP Toolkit (an XLSX document), located on BC Stats' website. It includes tables for all the indicators of the LAEP project, including employment, income, Income Dependency, Location Quotients, and economic multipliers for local areas and regional districts in British Columbia. It includes some ancillary data: tables which define the geographical classifications used in the project; the industry classifications; and a set of files that contain the original source data from the census (by area, detailed industries, and year) that has been cleaned to a level sufficient for input-output modelling.
local-area-economic-profiles-dataset.m: This is the final result of the LAEP project, which created an economic input-output model from data in the 2011, 2016 and 2021 censuses. The project released preliminary results in 2023. Depending on interest and available resources, it may be updated when future census data becomes available.

local-government-boundaries-road-centrel.d:
A spatial layer of polygon features representing Local Government jurisdictions of BC. The layer is composed of three groupings of government; Municipalities; Indian Reserves; First Nations Land Claim Settlements. The geometry is road-centreline aligned to the DRA 2 road network.

The Local Government Boundaries in this dataset are for use in delineating Elections BC's electoral boundaries, and may not be accurate. For the official, and legally defined administrative boundaries of local government areas, please refer to the following datasets:

https://catalogue.data.gov.bc.ca/dataset/legally-defined-administrative-areas-of-bc-internal
local-government-boundaries-road-centrel.m: Electoral Geography Division, Elections BC. Converted from Informix/DB2 to ESRI file geodatabase feature class by Elections BC.

c: MUNICIPALITY REGION ID is a system generated unique identification number.
REGION_TYPE is the classification of the local government region. Possible values are Regional District, Municipality, Indian Reserve and First Nations Settlement Area
INCORPORATION STATUS indicates whether the region represents an incorporated region ("INCORPORATED"), a First Nation ("FIRST NATION"), or regional district electoral area ("REGIONAL DISTRICT EA")

local-government-offices.d: Local Government Offices is a point dataset identifying local government offices in British Columbia.
local-government-offices.m: The location of local government offices is tracked in the sites database at GeoBC. This database identifies the physical location of the building or the access point to the property (for emergency response). This dataset is updated at the beginning of each month.

c: FACILITY_NAME is the name of the name of the government office, e.g., Haisla Resource Centre.
KEYWORDS contains text strings supplied by the Custodian, to be used for search/query purposes. Keywords are separated by the ; delimiter.
STREET_ADDRESS is a free form expression of the site descriptor (e.g., unit) and the civic building number / street / street indicator portion of an address, e.g., Unit 1, 123 Main Street East.

LOCALITY is the name of the municipality, community, Federal Indian Reserve (IR), subdivision, regional district, indigenous land or natural feature the occupant site is located in, e.g., Victoria, Saanich IR 1, Capital Regional District.
MAILING_ADDRESS contains an address string, not a parsed address. It is the address that will be displayed for presentation purposes, e.g., 32900 Marshall Road, Abbotsford, BC
WEBSITE_URL contains the link to the Home page of the Occupant's Website
IMAGE_URL contains a full URL link to a picture of the Occupant's Location.
LATITUDE is the geographic coordinate, in decimal degrees (dd.dddddd), of the location of the feature as measured from the equator, e.g., 55.323653
LONGITUDE is the geographic coordinate, in decimal degrees (-ddd.dddddd), of the location of the feature as measured from the prime meridian, e.g., -123.093544

PHYSICAL_ADDRESS contains the civic or non-civic address as a single string, structured according to the specification of the Physical Address and Geocoding Standard, e.g., 420 GORGE RD E, VICTORIA, BC.
DATE_UPDATED contains the date that the Occupant data was updated in the Occupant structure (system-generated)
SITE_GEOCODED_IND contains a Flag/indicator (Y/N) that the Occupant Physical Address has been geo-coded by the DataBC Address Geocoder and the results provide a valid site address, e.g., Y, N
SOURCE_DATA_ID is a unique occupant id either supplied by the source data system or produced by GSR, depending on the value of SUPPLIED_SOURCE_ID_IND
CUSTODIAN_ORG_DESCRIPTION contains the name or description of the custodial organization (usually Ministry and Branch)
BUSINESS_CATEGORY_CLASS designates the category of business, i.e., LocalGovernmentOffices
BUSINESS_CATEGORY_DESCRIPTION is the description that applies to its corresponding BUSINESS_CATEGORY_CLASS. E.g. Tourist accommodations for class accommodationFoodServices.accommodations.
OCCUPANT_TYPE_DESCRIPTION contains the description of the occupant type, e.g. Hospital
SHAPE is the column used to reference the spatial coordinates defining the feature.

SEQUENCE_ID contains a value to distinguish occupant instances. Where a single occupant can have multiple instances (representing different services, for example), this field distinguishes this occupant instance from other instances of the same or different occupants.
SE_ANNO_CAD_DATA is a binary column used by spatial tools to store annotation, curve features and CAD data when using the SDO_GEOMETRY storage data type.

local-health-area-boundaries.d:
Local Health Area (LHA) boundaries; 2022 boundary configuration.

The LHAs are a mutually exclusive and exhaustive classification of the land area in BC. LHAs are contiguous (land area is geographically adjacent) and fit within an existing geographical hierarchy structure, e.g., cannot violate higher-level geography boundaries such as the Health Service Delivery Areas (HSDA) and Health Authorities (HA).
local-health-area-boundaries.m:
Local Health Area boundaries have been updated to version 2022. This version includes only minor digitizing improvements to ensure consistency with the updated Community Health Service Area boundaries and to resolve small digitizing errors such as slivers. No other changes have been made to LHA boundaries in this version.

In April 2019, the Ministry of Health updated some provincial health regions and introduced the Community Health Service Area (CHSA). At this time LHA numbers were changed to align with other Ministry geographies and and some LHA names were altered to better represent the regional geography.

These LHAs were based on the 1997 version, at which time the Ministry of Health redefined the provincial health regions. Prior to this date the province was divided into 80 Local Health Areas (LHA) which were used for analytical purposes. They originally evolved from school …

Legally defined Local Trust Area polygons were drawn from metes and bounds descriptions as written in Letters Patent for the Local Trust Areas in the province of British Columbia.

c: CUSTODIAN_ORG_DESCRIPTION contains the name or description of the custodial organization (usually Ministry and Branch)

OCCUPANT_TYPE_DESCRIPTION contains the description of the occupant type, e.g. Hospital
SOURCE_DATA_ID is a unique occupant id either supplied by the source data system or produced by GSR, depending on the value of SUPPLIED_SOURCE_ID_IND
SUPPLIED_SOURCE_ID_IND is an indicator of whether the source data id was supplied by the supplier (Y) or DataBC (N)
OCCUPANT_NAME is a business name that can identify the occupant who provides the BC Government or BC Government related services to public.
DESCRIPTION describes the Occupant in more detail

PHYSICAL_ADDRESS contains the civic or non-civic address as a single string, structured according to the specification of the Physical Address and Geocoding Standard, e.g., 420 GORGE RD E, VICTORIA, BC.

The Major Projects Inventory (MPI), which is published quarterly, lists all major projects that are proposed, planned or underway in British Columbia. These are projects with a capital cost of at least $20 million each within the Lower Mainland and projects valued at $15 million or more in the rest of B.C. This is a point layer.

To view the Major Projects Inventory in the BC Economic Atlas [click here]( http://maps.gov.bc.ca/ess/hm/bcea/?catalogLayers=5178)

marine-ecosections-coastal-resource-info.d: Marine Ecosection classification for coastal and offshore British Columbia. The Marine Ecosections are: Johnstone Strait; Continental Slope; Dixon Entrance; Hecate Strait; Queen Charlotte Strait; Juan de Fuca Strait; North Coast Fjords; Queen Charlotte Sound; Strait of Georgia; Subarctic Pacific; Transitional Pacific; and Vancouver Island Shelf. The British Columbia Marine Ecological Classification (BCMEC) is a hierarchical classification that delineates Provincial marine areas into Ecozones, Ecoprovinces, Ecoregions and Ecosections. The classification was developed from previous Federal and Provincial marine ecological classifications which were based on 1:2,000,000 scale information. The BCMEC has been developed for marine and coastal planning, resource management and a Provincial marine protected areas strategy. A new, smaller level of classification termed ecounits developed using 1:250,000 scale depth, current, exposure, subsurface relief and substrate was created to verify the larger ecosections, and to delineate their boundaries. CRIMS is a legacy dataset of BC coastal resource data that was acquired in a systematic and synoptic manner from 1979 and was intermittently updated throughout the years. Resource information was collected in nine study areas using a peer-reviewed provincial Resource Information Standards Committee consisting of DFO Fishery Officers, First Nations, and other subject matter experts. There are currently no plans to update this legacy data.

mental-health-and-substance-use-health-s.d:
The HealthLink BC Mental Health and Substance Use (MHSU) data set includes the following:

Programs that offer early intervention, transitional care or other services that supplement and facilitate primary and adjunctive therapies; which offer community mental health education programs; or which link people who are in need of treatment with appropriate providers.

Programs that provide preventive, diagnostic and treatment services in a variety of community and hospital-based settings to help people achieve, maintain and enhance a state of emotional well-being, personal empowerment and the skills to cope with everyday demands without excessive stress or reliance on alcohol or other drugs. Treatment may include emotional support, introspection and problem-solving assistance using a variety of modalities and approaches, and medication, as needed, for individuals who have a substance use disorder involving alcohol and/or other drugs or for people who range from experiencing difficult life transitions or problems in coping with daily living to those with severe, chronic mental illnesses that seriously impact their lives.

migration-by-development-region-and-regi.d:
Mobility refers to the movement of individuals on a geographic basis, whether it’s international migration between B.C. and the rest of the world or inter-provincial migration between B.C. and other Canadian jurisdictions. The term mobility encompasses those statistics that show the number of migrants, where they’re going to and where they’re coming from.

Note: As part of the May 2024 update, Statistics Canada revised its calculation methods for estimating the numbers of emigrants and returning emigrants going back to census year 2016-17. Before 2016-17, short-term emigrants and short-term returning emigrants are included in the “Net Temporary Emigrants” component. From 2016-17 and after, they are included in the "Emigrants" and "Returning Emigrants" components using a different estimation methodology than previously. Due to this change, the "Net Temporary Emigrants" component is not calculated from 2016-17 onwards. Emigrant and returning emigrant estimates for periods before 2016-17 are not entirely comparable to subsequent estimates.

GeoFile 2020-11 is a re-release of all 120 profiles in one collection.

minfile-inventory-database.d:
Mineral Inventory describes the extent and volume of the reserve contained within a mineral deposit described by its referenced MINFILE_File record. MINFILE contains geological, location and economic information on 15,142 metallic, industrial mineral and coal occurrences in British Columbia. The database is used by government, industry and academia for resource management, land-use planning, exploration and research.

The Inventory 'Reserve' category is used only for an inventory in an operating mine or a mine near production. Ore reserves are reported as Proven, Probable and Possible. The Resource category is used for all other inventories. Resources are reported as Measured, Indicated and Inferred. A combination of categories is reported as Combined. If the category is not known then Unclassified is used. Sample data can be entered using the Assay/Analysis category. The reserves/resources are reported in tonnes with the grade of commodities.

In general, the inventory is identified by occurrence, zone name and year. There may be an unlimited number of ore zones per occurrence. In addition, each zone name may have inventory for each category. Each ore zone can have a maximum of two inventory calculations per year, per category (e.g., Calculation A & B). This allows for changes in calculations due to grade-tonnage relationships; calculation A may be high-grade low tonnage while calculation B may reflect a low-grade tonnage. Generally, only data for the most recent year is …

minfile-production-database.d:
MINFILE contains geological, location and economic information on 15,142 metallic, industrial mineral and coal occurrences in British Columbia. The database is used by government, industry and academia for resource management, land-use planning, exploration and research.

Production is linked by the MINFILE Number, and information such as production year. Information on either ore mined (in tonnes) or ore milled (in tonnes) are captured. Commodity production is entered with precious metals quoted in grams and base metals or other commodities quoted in kilograms. If there are no figures for tonnes milled the field will be blank. Comments are added to clarify information reported in the production field for any given year. Historic production records are provided by the Mines and Minerals Division of the Ministry of Energy, Mines and Petroleum Resources.
minfile-production-database.m: MINFILE contains over 16,000 metallic, industrial mineral and coal occurrences for British Columbia. Each of these occurrences contain 84 data elements describing mineral deposits in terms of geography, geology and economics. Started out as a card file, then to VAX, then to a microcomputer application, and finally to a web-based searchable database, with display on interactive maps.

Culverts that are greater than or equal to 3m in diameter are stored in the MoT Bridge Structure Road Dataset. It is a Point feature

ministry-of-transportation-mot-rest-area.d: A Rest Area is a developed roadside area for the use of the traveling public which must contain a washroom, and often has litter receptacles, picnic tables and other facilities. It is a Point feature

c: REST AREA ID is a system generated identifier to ensure row uniqueness. This is a primary key field.
CHRIS REST AREA ID contains the identifier of the rest area inventory item derived by the CHRIS application. E.g., 2455305
ADMIN UNIT CODE contains the MoT Service Area identifier. There are 28 service areas in MoT's jurisdiction. Each Service Area represents a geographic area within the province. E.g., 13

ADMIN UNIT NAME contains the MoT Service Area Name identifier. There are 28 service areas names in MoT's jurisdiction. Each Service Area Name represents a geographic area within the province. E.g., Lower Mainland
CROSS SECTION POSITION contains the cross sectional position of rest area in relationship to the road. E.g., Right of Way - Left, Division of Travel/End of Road, Shoulder - Left etc.
REST AREA NAME indicates the name of the rest area. E.g., 22 Peaceview Rest Area
REST AREA NUMBER indicates the MoT rest area identification number, utilized for identification by the Ministry Districts or Service areas. E.g., R0147
REST AREA CLASS contains a physical description of the MoT rest area class type. E.g., Rest Area Maintenance Class(RAM) Class A, RAM Class B, RAM Class C.

ASSOCIATED NUMBERED ROUTE is the numbered route on which the Rest Area is directly accessed from. If there is no associated numbered route then the Road Name is displayed in the Distance from Municipality attribute followed by the kilometre distance from the closest Municipality. e.g., 99
DISTANCE FROM MUNICIPALITY is the Distance in kilometres from the closest Municipality to the Rest Area. e.g., 28.7km North of Victoria
NUMBER OF TOILETS indicates the number of toilets in the rest area.
TOILET TYPE is a physical description of the type of toilets in the Rest Area. e.g., CH(Chemical), CO(Compost), Flush, Pit, Other
WHEELCHAIR ACCESS TOILET IND indicates whether a Rest Area has wheelchair accessible toilets or not. e.g., Yes or No
NUMBER OF TABLES indicates the number of tables in the rest area.
NUMBER OF STANDARD BARRELS indicates the number of standard barrels in the rest area.
NUMBER OF BEAR PROOF BARRELS indicates the number of bear proof barrels in the rest area.
POWER TYPE is a physical description of the power available in a Rest Area. e.g., Battery, Electrical, Generator, Solar or No Power
POWER RESPONSIBILITY indicates who is responsible for the power in a Rest Area. e.g., Contractor, Province or NA
DIRECTION OF TRAFFIC is the direction the traffic is heading when approaching the Rest Area (i.e., the rest area would be on the passenger side of the vehicle). e.g., NB, SB, EB or WB
ACCESS RESTRICTION indicates which direction does NOT have access to the Rest Area. e.g., NB, SB, EB, WB or No Restriction
DECELERATION LANE IND Indicates whether a deceleration lane exists or not for a Rest Area. e.g., Yes or No
ACCELERATION LANE IND Indicates whether an acceleration lane exists or not for a Rest Area. e.g., Yes or No
DIRECT ACCESS IND indicates whether the Rest Area is accessible directly from the Numbered Route (i.e., not down a frontage road or other side road). e.g., Yes or No
ACCOM COMMERCIAL TRUCKS IND indicates whether the Rest Area accommodates commercial trucks or not. e.g., Yes or No
OPEN YEAR ROUND IND indicates whether the Rest Area is open year round or not. e.g., Yes or No
ANNUAL OPEN DATE indicates the approximate annual open date (if applicable) in the Spring for the rest area (MM-DD).
ANNUAL CLOSE DATE indicates the approximate annual closing date (if applicable) in the Fall for the rest area (MM-DD)
CHRIS ANCHOR SECTON ID contains the CHRIS application internal unique identifier for the anchor section segment. E.g., 2777363
EVENT LOCATION contains the measure for the rest area along the anchor section. Measures are in Kilometer (km). E.g., 42.200 km
HIGHWAY NUMBER is the MoT Numbered Route identifier populated when the rest area is located on a MoT Numbered route. E.g., 99
